articles.title: African Leaders Urged to Invest Domestic Resources in Industrial Growth - liberianobserver.com
articles.summary: African Leaders Urged to Invest Domestic Resources in Industrial Growth  liberianobserver.com
articles.full_text:
African leaders have been urged to invest domestic financial resources in industrial development, local manufacturing and value addition to create jobs, strengthen economies and reduce dependence on external financing.
The call came during the Africa@WorldBank/IMF gathering in Bangkok on October 14, where policymakers, development finance executives, researchers and business leaders discussed strategies to accelerate industrialization and strengthen Africa’s role in global economic decision-making.
Participants stressed that African countries must move beyond exporting raw materials and expand local processing to retain more economic value on the continent.
World Trade Organization Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, who received the 2026 Trailblazer for Africa Award at the gathering, highlighted the continent’s natural wealth and the need to use it to support industrial growth.
Africa accounts for approximately 30 percent of the world’s critical minerals, she noted, but captures limited value when those resources are processed and manufactured elsewhere.
Okonjo-Iweala also pointed to the potential of domestic savings to finance development. She cited approximately US$250 billion in pension assets across Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa, saying regulatory reforms could help direct more of these funds toward infrastructure, industrial development and other productive investments.
Greater mobilization of domestic capital could help African countries reduce reliance on external borrowing amid high financing costs and mounting debt pressures.
She also stressed that reliable electricity and infrastructure are essential to industrial growth and business competitiveness.
Dr. Denis Foretia, Executive Chairman of the Nkafu Policy Institute and founder of the Denis and Lenora Foretia Foundation, urged African countries to learn from Thailand’s industrial transformation, including its development of electronics and automobile manufacturing.
“Just two generations ago, Thailand was a low-income economy selling raw produce,” Foretia said. “Africa can follow the same path.”
He cited the cashew industry as an example of the value Africa loses by exporting raw products. Less than 15 percent of African cashew production is processed locally, according to figures cited at the gathering.
Expanding local processing, participants said, could create jobs, increase export earnings and allow African producers to retain a greater share of the value generated from their products.
A panel on industrialization, value chains and employment also examined the importance of financing, energy access and responsible borrowing.
Catherine Mithia of the African Forum and Network on Debt and Development highlighted the need for borrowing that supports sustainable economic returns, while Rajneesh Bhuee, Just Transition Lead at Recourse, said foreign investment alone would not resolve Africa’s manufacturing challenges without reliable energy infrastructure.
Dr. Eliya Zulu of the African Institute for Development Policy also participated in the discussion, moderated by Bruno Ittia of the Denis and Lenora Foretia Foundation.
Other sessions focused on debt management, gender-responsive economic policies, Africa-Asia trade, digital connectivity and the implementation of development plans. Participants explored ways to improve market access, strengthen regulatory cooperation and expand cross-border payment systems.
The session “Africa Transforming Africa: From Ambition to Action” examined obstacles to development, including financing gaps, weak coordination and institutional challenges. Participants included Mavis Owusu-Gyamfi of the African Center for Economic Transformation, Dr. Hodan Osman Abdi of the Somali Development and Reconstruction Bank, African Union Commissioner Francisca Tatchouop Belobe and AfroChampions Initiative co-founder Edem Adzogenu. Guinea’s Planning Minister Ismael Nabe delivered introductory remarks.
The gathering also highlighted the need for greater African participation in international economic policymaking. Foretia said the Africa@WorldBank/IMF initiative aims to ensure that African priorities are better represented in decisions affecting the continent.
“Too often, Africa’s priorities are discussed—usually not by Africans, and without Africans at the table,” he said at the initiative’s April 2026 gathering in Washington.
Other participants in Bangkok included South Africa’s Deputy Minister of Finance, Dr. David Masondo; Mauritania’s Central Bank Governor, Mohamed Lemine Dhehby; and Development Bank of Southern Africa Chief Executive Officer Boitumelo Mosako.
The initiative brings together African policy and research institutions, including the Nkafu Policy Institute, the African Center for Economic Transformation, the Partnership for Economic Policy and the Centre for the Study of the Economies of Africa.
Its next gatherings are scheduled for April 14 and October 6, 2027, in Washington, DC.
The discussions emphasized that turning Africa’s natural wealth and domestic savings into jobs and economic growth will require sustained investment in local industries, reliable infrastructure and policies that support value addition.

articles.title: The VEFTA agreement expands export opportunities and attracts high-quality investment. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: The VEFTA agreement expands export opportunities and attracts high-quality investment.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
To translate VEFTA commitments into tangible benefits, Vietnam not only needs to quickly complete the procedures for implementing the agreement but also needs to enhance its competitiveness and meet the required standards.
The official signing of the Vietnam-EFTA Free Trade Agreement (VEFTA) between Vietnam and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) on October 18, 2026, concludes 14 years of negotiations and opens up further opportunities for exports, investment, and technological cooperation with four developed European economies .
However, to translate commitments into tangible benefits, Vietnam not only needs to quickly complete the procedures for implementing the agreement but also needs to enhance its competitiveness, meet stringent standards, and improve its ability to utilize preferential treatment.
In the presence of General Secretary and President To Lam, on October 18th, Minister of Industry and Trade Le Manh Hung, along with representatives from Switzerland, Norway , Iceland, and Liechtenstein, signed the VEFTA Agreement in Hanoi.
This is Vietnam's 18th FTA, marking a new step in its strategy of international economic integration, in the context of global trade facing pressure from protectionism, geopolitical competition, and fluctuations in supply chains.
Minister of Industry and Trade Le Manh Hung emphasized that the signing of the agreement is a significant milestone in economic and trade relations between Vietnam and EFTA countries. The agreement, signed after 14 years of negotiations and 21 working sessions, demonstrates the political determination and persistent efforts of all parties.
“The Vietnam-EFTA Agreement opens up new avenues for cooperation in trade in goods, services, investment, and sustainable development. Tariff preferences will facilitate the expansion of Vietnamese markets and enhance competitiveness for Vietnamese goods, while also helping EFTA businesses more effectively exploit the potential of the Vietnamese market. Rules of origin also facilitate production linkages and supply chain connections between Europe and Southeast Asia,” Minister Le Manh Hung emphasized.
Initiated in 2012, the VEFTA negotiations spanned 21 sessions, with a seven-year interruption. The two sides finally announced the conclusion of negotiations on July 2, 2026, before officially signing the agreement in October 2026. This lengthy process reflects the complexity of a comprehensive agreement between Vietnam and developed economies, requiring a balance between trade interests, market openness, and regulatory standards.
Notably, VEFTA covers many areas such as trade in goods, services, investment, rules of origin, customs procedures, technical barriers, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, intellectual property, government procurement, and sustainable development.
Intellectual property is a noteworthy area, with commitments to the protection and enforcement of copyrights, trademarks, inventions, industrial designs, geographical indications, and trade secrets. These regulations provide a legal basis for trade and investment while also requiring Vietnam to continue improving its institutions and enhancing its compliance capacity.
Norwegian Ambassador to Vietnam Stein Iversen assessed the results achieved after 14 years as demonstrating the strong commitment, perseverance, and determination of all parties, while affirming the importance of the Vietnam-EFTA cooperation. One of the most obvious benefits is that the agreement will create a more level playing field for Norwegian seafood products, especially salmon. This is a crucial sector accounting for a large proportion of bilateral trade between the two countries.
The tariff reductions under the agreement will facilitate greater access for Norwegian seafood in the Vietnamese market. This means more and more Vietnamese consumers will be able to enjoy high-quality Norwegian salmon and other seafood at affordable prices. Conversely, it is hoped that Norwegians will soon be able to enjoy more of Vietnam's coffee and tropical fruits.
You may also like
Furthermore, maritime transport, shipbuilding, fisheries, green energy, and marine economic sectors have been important areas of cooperation between the two countries in recent years. Improved market access, along with a stable and transparent trade framework, will build confidence for businesses to invest and expand their operations in Vietnam. In particular, the FTA will help Vietnam become an attractive destination for businesses looking to diversify their markets and supply chains.
According to Silvan Wildhaber, President of the Swiss Business Federation (Economiesuisse), for Swiss businesses, the agreement provides better market access, greater legal certainty, and more favorable conditions for investment. For Vietnamese businesses, the agreement opens opportunities for deeper participation in international value chains, access to advanced technology, and enhanced cooperation with innovative Swiss partners.
However, signing the agreement is not the destination but the starting point, because the success of a free trade agreement is not only measured by the signing of the document but also by the opportunities the agreement creates in daily business operations.
The effectiveness of the agreement must be demonstrated through new orders, partnerships formed, and expanded investment. Therefore, the parties need to ensure transparent regulations, streamlined procedures, consistent application, and regular dialogue between regulatory agencies and the business community.
Experts point out that with VEFTA, Vietnam has gained four new partners, adding to its network of 17 FTAs already signed with 65 countries and territories. Along with the Vietnam-EU Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA) and the Vietnam-UK Free Trade Agreement (UKVFTA), VEFTA expands Vietnam's preferential trade framework in developed economies in Western Europe, creating more options for businesses to diversify markets and reduce dependence on a few traditional partners.
The four EFTA countries have a combined population of only about 15 million, but they are all high-income economies with significant purchasing power and stringent market standards.
By 2025, bilateral trade between Vietnam and the EFTA is expected to reach approximately 4.8 billion euros, with Vietnam having a trade surplus of around 2.5 billion euros. The current scale of trade shows significant room for expansion, especially as tariff preferences are implemented and Vietnamese businesses better meet market standards.
According to the agreement, EFTA will completely eliminate import tariffs on industrial and seafood products originating from Vietnam as soon as the agreement comes into effect. For agricultural products, EFTA countries will grant preferential treatment according to a schedule appropriate to the sensitivity level of each item. Conversely, Vietnam will eliminate most import tariffs on industrial and seafood products from EFTA within a maximum period of 11 years.
These commitments create additional advantages for key export sectors, including seafood, textiles, footwear, wood products, and some agricultural products. However, the benefits lie not only in reduced tariffs but also in the ability to build long-term supply relationships with importers, distributors, and industrial partners in markets with high demands for quality, transparency, and sustainable development.
Swiss Ambassador to Vietnam Thomas Gass stated that the agreement establishes a modern framework for trade and investment cooperation, contributing to strengthening economic relations between EFTA and Vietnam. Furthermore, the agreement aims to improve market access, reduce trade barriers, enhance legal certainty for businesses, and promote sustainable and inclusive growth.
Therefore, the EFTA-Vietnam FTA is expected to boost trade, investment, and technology transfer between Vietnam and EFTA countries. The agreement will also facilitate investment in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, precision engineering, machinery, clean technology, and high-quality food, while supporting Vietnam's continued deep integration into global supply chains.
You may also like
Ms. Nguyen Thi Hoang Thuy, Commercial Counselor of the Vietnamese Trade Office in Sweden, concurrently covering Denmark, Norway, Iceland, and Latvia, emphasized that the Vietnam-EFTA Free Trade Agreement goes beyond a tariff reduction agreement. This message affirms Vietnam's continued commitment to deep international economic integration, market diversification, partner diversification, and improving the quality of trade relations with developed economies.
With the Vietnam-EFTA Free Trade Agreement, businesses need to see not only opportunities to increase exports but also opportunities to upgrade themselves. The EFTA market sets very high standards, but these are in line with Vietnam's new development orientation of increasing added value, improving the quality of growth, and participating more deeply in sustainable supply chains.
To effectively capitalize on these opportunities, Ms. Nguyen Thi Hoang Thuy noted that businesses need to focus on three factors: standardization, transparency, and perseverance. Standardization must be implemented consistently from products and processes to documentation and contracts; transparency requires clearly showing the origin of raw materials, production standards, emissions, working conditions, and social responsibility.
In particular, businesses need to persistently build credibility, strengthen trust, and develop long-term cooperative relationships with partners, rather than expecting immediate results. These are crucial conditions for Vietnamese businesses not only to access but also to establish themselves and expand their market share in the EFTA market in the long term.

articles.title: CHANGAN Marks 3 Years in Thailand, Reinforcing Thailand’s Strategic Role as Its SEA Headquarters and Largest Overseas Manufacturing and Export Base - ThaiPR.NET
articles.summary: CHANGAN Marks 3 Years in Thailand, Reinforcing Thailand’s Strategic Role as Its SEA Headquarters and Largest Overseas Manufacturing and Export Base  ThaiPR.NET
articles.full_text:
CHANGAN Automobile, a leader in new energy vehicle (NEV) technology, marked its third year in Thailand with “CHANGAN DAY 2026: GO FURTHER TOGETHER,” reaffirming its commitment to establish Thailand as its Southeast Asia headquarters and its largest overseas manufacturing and export base. Over the past three years, CHANGAN has sold more than 35,000 vehicles in Thailand, with annual sales rising from approximately 5,000 units in 2024 to 14,000 units in 2025, and a target of 30,000 units in 2026, representing an average annual growth rate of over 100%. Its CHANGAN Automobile Rayong Factory, the company’s first NEV production base outside China, now manufactures models including the DEEPAL S05 and NEVO Q05, with exports of 6,000 units from Thailand expected to serve 18 countries and regions in 2026.
Mr. Ricky Wu (Wu Xiaokang), Vice President and Customer Officer, CHANGAN Auto Southeast Asia, said:
“Over the past three years, we have moved forward step by step, building a strong foundation for the future. In our first year, we introduced our brands to Thailand. Thai consumers got to know CHANGAN, DEEPAL, and AVATR. This was the first step in keeping our promise to build a long-term presence in Thailand. In our second year, our overseas new-energy vehicle plant began operations. New models rolled off the production line and entered the Thai market. We kept our promise to invest in local manufacturing. In our third year, we continued to turn our promises into action. Our brands and products have gained more recognition and trust from Thai consumers. Throughout this journey, we have stayed focused on steady and responsible growth. We believe in doing things well, step by step, and building a strong foundation for the future. Looking back on our three years in Thailand, I would sum up our journey in one sentence: time will tell.”
ADVERTISEMENT
“On behalf of CHANGAN, I would like to thank the Royal Thai Government, the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI), the Customs Department, the Excise Department, the Office of Industrial Economics, the Thailand Automotive Institute, the Automotive Human Resource Development Academy, our customers, business partners, the media and every employee who has been part of our success over the past three years.”
3 Years, 9 Models: Meeting Thai Consumers’ Needs
ADVERTISEMENT
Over the past three years, CHANGAN has launched nine new-energy vehicle models in Thailand under two brands: CHANGAN, whose product series include DEEPAL, NEVO and LUMIN, and the luxury brand AVATR. The lineup ranges from practical, value-focused EVs to premium and luxury models, and several have won Car of the Year and design awards from leading Thai media. CHANGAN develops tailor-made products designed specifically for Thai road conditions, climate and driving habits. This momentum is reflected in the Thai-built DEEPAL S05, which has ranked first in monthly electric SUV registrations. The NEVO Q05, launched in mid-2026, also received 2,200 bookings in its first week.
Made in Thailand, Sold Worldwide
ADVERTISEMENT
The CHANGAN Rayong plant was built in 18 months with a total investment over THB 10 billion, which includes product development, and officially launched in May 2025. It covers all key production processes, from body welding and painting to final assembly and battery-pack production, allowing more key EV components to be made locally. Over the past three years, CHANGAN has grown its network of Thai parts suppliers from more than 300 to 413, bringing more technology, skills and production capabilities to Thailand, from product testing and development to key components and vehicle manufacturing.
Thailand also serves as CHANGAN’s strategic production base for exporting EVs to right-hand-drive markets worldwide. The first batch of Thai-built DEEPAL S05 was shipped to Europe in 2025, and CHANGAN expects exports from Thailand to reach 6,000 vehicles in 2026, serving 18 countries and regions. This role is driven by CHANGAN Automobile’s Vast Ocean Plan 2.0, which aims to evolve CHANGAN from a Chinese car exporter into a global automotive brand with fully integrated business, manufacturing and operations in overseas markets, targeting overseas sales of 1.5 million units by 2030.
Better Service and Greater Responsibility
CHANGAN has developed a comprehensive after-sales system covering its call center, technical center and parts center, achieving a first-time fix rate of 97.3%. Its after-sales technical center in Thailand also supports 17 countries and regions across Southeast Asia, reinforcing Thailand’s role as a regional service hub. Together with NING SERVICE by CATL, CHANGAN has invested more than THB 30 million in the CHANGAN Battery and E-Drive Service Center, which can service more than 40 vehicles per month across batteries, electric motors and electronic control systems, helping extend battery life and reduce the cost of full battery replacement, while transferring technical skills from China to Thai technicians.
CHANGAN currently employs 2,143 people in Thailand, more than 90% of whom are Thai, with more Thai colleagues taking on middle and senior management roles. Across its value chain, the company has helped create more than 30,000 jobs.
The Next Three Years: Going Further Together with Thailand
The first three years mark only the beginning of CHANGAN’s journey in Thailand. Over the next three years, the company aims to grow its business to more than three times its current level and to become one of Thailand’s leading and most responsible automotive brands. Its key priorities include:
- More choices for customers: introducing 12 major new models designed for local needs, so that customers with different needs and budgets can find a CHANGAN vehicle that suits them.
- Stronger local manufacturing and Thai talent: bringing more high-value and key components into local production at Rayong under CHANGAN’s global standards, employing more than 3,000 people in Thailand by 2030, increasing the number of Thai managers and training more than 300 local technical professionals.
- Made in Thailand, for the world: CHANGAN’s first overseas NEV plant began operations in Rayong in May 2025. It now produces the DEEPAL S05 and NEVO Q05 and makes Thailand a production base for export markets worldwide.
- Closer service and care: expanding the service network to more than 150 locations nationwide, with regional BP service centers, more certified body and paint centers and L3 technical repair centers, building battery-cell-level repair capability for faster, more professional service.
- Growing together with partners and society: providing stronger support for dealers and service partners, and advancing ESG initiatives, including tree planting with King Mongkut’s Institute of Technology, free NEV training materials for the Ministry of Labour and partner schools, special rainy-season service support, and EV battery fire emergency drills with local fire departments.
Putting Customers at the Heart of Everything
From its Rayong plant and local supply chain to its service network and Thai workforce, every investment CHANGAN makes in Thailand serves one purpose: giving Thai customers the confidence to choose CHANGAN. Looking ahead to the next ten years and beyond, the company is committed to delivering a consistent ownership experience for every customer, across both brands and all product series, through its nationwide network of CHANGAN and AVATR showrooms and service centers.
He added: “Our success over the past three years comes from the trust of Thai consumers. We believe the automotive market is not about competing on price, but about the long-term value a company delivers to its customers. Vehicles should offer a wide range of choices to meet different needs, be designed for Thai roads and climate, and fit Thai lifestyles. We want CHANGAN EVs to be more than vehicles: we want them to be travel companions that make life easier and provide peace of mind, allowing every customer to feel confident throughout their CHANGAN ownership journey.”
Thailand is where CHANGAN’s global journey truly began, and it will remain a key base for the company’s future growth, bringing the innovation and quality of Made in Thailand to more markets around the world.
Mr. Ricky Wu added: “Thailand’s 30@2030 is a national policy designed to drive and promote the electric vehicle (EV) industry in Thailand. CHANGAN’s business direction aligns with the Thailand policy and the company is ready to help drive the continued growth of the Thai automotive industry. Three years ago, we committed to investing in Thailand. Today, we are taking the next step by walking hand in hand with Thai society and partners to build a shared future. CHANGAN does not see Thailand merely as a market for selling cars, but as a key partner in developing the automotive industry, creating economic opportunities and raising the potential of Thai people together.”

articles.title: Greenfield investment to drive FDI - China Daily Global Edition
articles.summary: Greenfield investment to drive FDI  China Daily Global Edition
articles.full_text:
Greenfield investment to drive FDI
By Shi Jing in Shanghai | China Daily | Updated: 2026-10-22 09:16
Greenfield investment, a category of foreign direct investment wherein a company constructs new facilities and other assets in a foreign market, will replace mergers and acquisitions to become Chinese companies' most sought-after outbound approach amid their continued global expansion steps, according to a think tank report.
Compiled by the CF40 Institute — the research arm of the China Finance 40 Forum — "China's Economy toward a New Paradigm" was released on Tuesday as part of the Bund Summit 2026.
While going global will continue to be a major development trajectory for Chinese firms, its form will evolve from the traditional emphasis on goods exports to overseas investment, localized production and the establishment of supply chains abroad.
In other words, overseas expansion will be increasingly characterized by building new factories and production lines as well as establishing entities abroad rather than acquiring existing assets, according to the report, which addressed topics such as China's economic drivers, major economic trends and policy implications.
To make these new entities operational, companies need to build local workforces, supplier networks, financing channels, compliance systems and sales networks from the ground up. The relationship between Chinese firms and offshore economies will therefore extend beyond mere trade and into overseas production, said Guo Kai, executive president and senior fellow at the CF40 Institute.
The dominance of greenfield investment is by no means accidental but rather a result of companies' active response to the evolving global trade environment, said Guo.
Tariffs and trade barriers have mounted over the past few years, especially for automobiles, basic materials and energy — China's current major export drivers. The rising Chinese industrial competence in new energy vehicles, batteries and solar products has resulted in more tariffs, investment reviews and localization requirements, Guo added.
To preserve existing overseas markets, companies need to locate part of production closer to end-consumer markets, set up local factories, hire local workers, procure local components and establish offshore sales networks, he said.
The changing domestic market landscape has also prompted companies to attach greater importance to greenfield investment. Although China's manufacturing capacity built up over the past several years remains substantial, domestic demand growth has slowed, making it a bit difficult for Chinese companies to sustain rapid growth through overreliance on the domestic market. Real estate adjustments and fiscal pressures have also constrained the scope for rapid expansion of domestic demand.
Against this backdrop, Chinese companies with technological, cost and supply-chain advantages naturally look to overseas markets as new sources of growth. Particularly in internationally competitive industries such as automobiles, new energy, and machinery and equipment, overseas expansion is no longer simply about selling products abroad, but more about reorganizing production, supply chains and global market presence, according to the report, which added that the accelerated overseas expansion of Chinese companies will lead to a longer-term change in the foundations of the renminbi's internationalization.
While the process used to rely more on China's large trade flows, the wider use of the yuan can be spurred by Chinese companies' rising investment, production and operations in overseas markets.
"The globalization of Chinese firms could become a new driver for the RMB's internationalization," said Guo.

Dozens of Israeli Air Force fighter jets conducted a sortie on Monday, flying as far as the Iranian border, according to Israeli and U.S. officials.
Why it matters: The operation, more than 800 miles away from Israel, took place a week before the Israeli elections and on the same day Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at Israel's Ovda Air Base. The sortie wasn't connected to Hegseth's visit.
While some Israeli and U.S. officials said the sortie wasn't unusual and that it was meant to deter Iran, it could have led to a miscalculation, triggering an Iranian response andreigniting the war.
Behind the scenes: The exercise involved dozens of fighter jets and refueling aircraft, the sources said.
It followed a flight path consistent with a potential strike against Iran, passing through Syrian and Iraqi airspace.
As the aircraft approached the Iranian border, they turned around and returned to Israel, the sources said.
The intrigue: U.S. officials said the Israelis knew that Iran's air defense systems would detect the sortie.
According to the sources, Israel notified the U.S. in advance and described the operation as a training exercise intended for "power projection" and aimed at deterring Iran from launching attacks against Israel ahead of the elections.
However, some U.S. sources said they had the impression that Israel was hoping the Iranians would fire at the aircraft, providing a justification for launching strikes against Iran.
Fox News reported on Tuesday that the Israeli Air Force conducted a drill towards Iran.
Driving the news: Last week, Axios reported that Netanyahu and President Trump discussed in early October the possibility of launching a major newoperation against Iran before the Israeli and U.S. elections.
Netanyahu told Trump he was concerned about Israeli intelligence indicating Iran was taking troubling steps to reconstitute its nuclear program.
Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir told Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine at the time that restarting the war in that timeframe could cause the Israeli elections to be postponed, given that Iran would probably retaliate, the sources said.
Trump initially seemed to be inclined to resume attacks, but then grew hesitant and eventually decided against Netanyahu's proposal.
State of play: An Israeli official said Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir will not allow any unjustified military activity that could undermine the Oct. 27 elections.
What he's saying: On Wednesday Netanyahu said at a military graduation ceremony that Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei "has decided to follow in his father's footsteps" and allowed Iranian scientists to move forward with building a nuclear weapon.
"He has taken the safety off, and Iran is once again trying to develop its bombs of death," Netanyahu said.
"Therefore, there is only one way to eliminate this threat once and for all: to overthrow the regime in Iran. And that is the directive I have given to the IDF, the Mossad and the security agencies," he added.

Information Collection Request Title:
Title V Maternal and Child Health Services Block Grant to States Program: Guidance and Forms for the Title V Application/Annual Report OMB No. 0915-0172—Revision.
Abstract:
The Title V Maternal and Child Health (MCH) Services Block Grant to States Program is authorized by Sections 501-509 of Title V of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 701-709). HRSA is updating the
Title V Maternal and Child Health Services Block Grant to States Program: Guidance and Forms for the Title V Application/Annual Report
(Guidance). This Guidance is used annually by the 50 states and nine jurisdictions (the District of Columbia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of Palau, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands; hereafter referred to as “state”) in applying for Block Grants under Title V of the Social Security Act and in preparing the required Annual Report. The updates being proposed by HRSA for this edition of the Guidance continue to support the federal-state partnership that is supported by the Title V MCH Services Block Grant and the state's role in developing a 5-Year Action Plan that addresses its individual priority needs. Updates to this edition of the Guidance are editorial and technical revisions based on feedback from the states in using the Guidance and Forms since January 2024, and by comments received from State Title V program leadership, national MCH leaders, other MCH stakeholders, and the public.
A 60-day notice published in the
Federal Register
on May 19, 2026, vol. 91, No. 96; pp. 29140-41 (91 FR 29140). The 60-day
Federal Register
Notice (FRN) stated that minor editorial corrections and clarifications were made to Form 7, Form 10, Form 12 instructions and the Glossary, and that updates were made to the short and long titles of the National Performance Measures to improve title accuracy and fulfill Government Accountability Office recommendations and align National Performance Measures with other HRSA program measures. However, the reference to Form 12 instructions in the 60-day FRN was a technical error; instead, the FRN should have referred to Form 11, to which additional minor clarifications were made.
HRSA received comments from five respondents (state Title V programs and other MCH stakeholders) on the proposed updates to the eleventh edition of the Guidance. The submitted responses included multiple comments. Of the five respondents, four respondents provided comments related to implementation of the guidance or the Title V Information System (TVIS) that would be addressed most effectively in the form of technical assistance, rather than adjusting the guidance instructions. Two respondents recommended expanding the definitions of budget-related glossary terms to

include additional examples for each category. HRSA considered all public comments as part of its deliberative process in finalizing updates to the eleventh edition of the
Title V Maternal and Child Health Services Block Grant to States Program: Guidance and Forms for the Title V Application/Annual Report.
A discussion of the public comments received during the 60-day comment period and HRSA's response to the comments is set below:
(1)
Organization and Structure of the Application/Annual Report Guidance.
Comments:
Some respondents expressed support for the Application/Annual Report Guidance reporting structure that was implemented as part of the tenth edition and maintained through this edition. Respondents provided additional comments related to combining various sections of the Application/Annual Report, such as: (1) Systems and Services for Children with Special Health Care Needs with Relationship with Medicaid; (2) Title V Purpose and Design, Organizational Structure, Impact of Organizational Structure, and Impact of Agency Capacity; (3) System of Care for Mothers, Infants, and Families with Systems and Services for Children with Special Health Care Needs; (4) How Title V Funds Support MCH Efforts and the Expenditures and Budget Narratives; (5) MCH Population Health and Wellbeing and State Description; (6) Impact of Organizational Structure, Impact of Agency Capacity, and Title V Workforce Capacity and Workforce Development; and (7) Title V Partnerships, Collaboration, and Coordination and Family and Community Partnerships.
HRSA Response:
HRSA will not adopt the recommendation to consolidate the identified sections, as each section requests distinct types of information or fulfills a legislative requirement. Consolidating sections increases the risk that important information may be left out or overlooked. HRSA also sought to minimize revisions in the eleventh edition of the guidance to provide State Title V programs sufficient time to implement and adjust to the Application/Annual Report reporting structure that was introduced in the tenth edition. AGENCY:
Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Announcement of public hearing and extension of comment period.
SUMMARY:
On July 3, 2025, FRA published notice that Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited (CPKC) petitioned FRA for relief from certain regulations concerning air brake testing. In this notice, FRA is announcing a public hearing to allow interested persons the opportunity to provide comments on the petition. FRA is also reopening the comment period to allow time for interested parties to submit comments on the petition or in response to views or information provided at the public hearing.
DATES:
(1) A public hearing will be held on November 18, 2026, from 1 p.m. (CDT) to 5 p.m. (CDT) in St. Paul, Minnesota, and through one or more internet links.
(2) Comments: FRA must receive comments on the petition, or in response to views or information provided at the public hearing, by December 18, 2026. FRA will consider comments received after that date to the extent practicable.
ADDRESSES:
Public Hearing:
The public hearing will allow for participation in person or virtually. For those appearing in person, the public hearing will be held at the CPKC Battle Creek Operations Building, 1010 Shop Road, St. Paul, MN 55106. For those participants wishing to make a statement at the public hearing, either in person or virtually, please contact FRA as described under the Public Participation Procedures heading in the
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
section of this document.
( printed page 66621)
Comments:
Comments related to this docket may be submitted by going to
https://www.regulations.gov
and following the online instructions for submitting comments.
Instructions:
All submissions must include the agency name and docket number. All comments received will be posted without change to
https://www.regulations.gov;
this includes any personal information. Please see the Privacy Act heading in the
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
section of this document for Privacy Act information related to any submitted comments or materials.
Docket:
For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to
https://www.regulations.gov
and follow the online instructions for accessing the docket.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Kar Gazarov, Deputy Staff Director, FRA Motive Power & Equipment Division, telephone: 904-776-5697, email:
kar.gazarov@dot.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The purpose of this hearing is to receive comments in response to a petition, received under part 211 of title 49 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), from CPKC for a waiver related to certain air brake testing regulations. By letter dated April 4, 2025, CPKC petitioned FRA for a waiver of compliance from §§ 232.5,
Definitions;
232.15,
Movement of defective equipment;
232.103(f),
General requirements for all train brake systems;
232.205(a),
Class I brake test—initial terminal inspection;
and 232.213(a)(6)(ii),
Extended haul trains.
CPKC also requests an exemption from the requirements of title 49, United States Code (U.S.C.), section 20303, which states that a rail vehicle with defective or insecure equipment may be moved to the nearest available place “at which the repairs can be made.”
The petitioner (CPKC) should be present at the hearing and prepared to present evidence to justify its request. Interested parties are invited to present statements and to offer information and views at the hearing. The hearing will be an informal, non-adversarial proceeding conducted by a representative FRA designates under FRA's Rules of Practice (49 CFR 211.25). Therefore, there will be no cross-examination of persons presenting statements or offering information. An FRA representative will make an opening statement outlining the scope of the hearing. Interested parties will then be provided with an opportunity to make initial statements. After all initial statements are completed, those persons wishing to make a brief rebuttal will be given the opportunity to do so, in the same order in which they made the initial statements. FRA will announce any additional procedures at the hearing.
There will be a court reporter to record and transcribe comments presented at the hearing. FRA will add the verbatim transcript of the discussions to the public docket in this proceeding.
Public Participation Procedures
Any person: (1) wishing to attend the hearing in person or virtually, (2) make a statement at the hearing either in-person or virtually, or (3) both, should notify FRA by contacting Kar Gazarov, Deputy Staff Director, FRA Motive Power & Equipment Division, by email at
kar.gazarov@dot.gov, no later than Thursday, November 12, 2026 providing the following information, as applicable:
(a) The name, affiliation or party represented, email address, and phone number of the participant.
(b) Whether the participant is attending in person or virtually.
(c) The subject(s) of the statement and/or presentation the participant wishes to make, and the amount of time requested.
(d) A copy of the oral statement and/or presentation, if available.
FRA reserves the right to limit participation in the hearing of persons who fail to follow the public participation procedures as outlined above, or additional procedures announced at the hearing. FRA also reserves the right to limit the duration of presentations, as necessary, to afford all persons the opportunity to speak, or to limit participation in the hearing of persons who exceed their allotted time or who discuss topics or issues outside the scope of the petition. Further, FRA reserves the right to limit in-person attendance at the hearing, as space is limited; preference in attendance will be provided to persons requesting to present statements in person.
FRA is committed to providing equal access to this meeting for all participants. If you need alternative formats or other reasonable accommodations to participate in this meeting, either in-person or virtually, please contact Kar Gazarov, Deputy Staff Director, FRA Motive Power & Equipment Division, by email at
kar.gazarov@dot.gov, no later than Thursday, November 12, 2026.
Extension of Comment Period
FRA is extending the comment period to December 18, 2026 to allow time for interested parties to submit written comments on the proposal or in response to views or information provided at the public hearing.

articles.title: Live Updates: U.S. reducing troop footprint in Middle East, sources say, as indirect talks on ceasefire proposal with Iran continue - CBS News
articles.summary: Live Updates: U.S. reducing troop footprint in Middle East, sources say, as indirect talks on ceasefire proposal with Iran continue  CBS NewsU.S. troops and diplomats evacuating Middle East posts, sources say  NBC NewsIran live updates: US military repositions personnel at Mideast bases, source says  ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and VideosPentagon weighs force posture, costs of rebuilding Middle East bases  Breaking DefenseU.S. reducing troop foot...
articles.full_text:
What to know about the Iran war today:
- The U.S. military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing regional threats from the Iran-backed Houthis and direct threats from Iran, sources tell CBS News Wednesday.
The latest attack targeted King Fahd International Airport in the eastern Saudi Arabian city of Dammam, killing at least one person and injuring eight others Wednesday evening, Saudi officials said.
- Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue over a seven-day ceasefire proposal that President last month, with the U.S. seeking new clauses.
- A senior official with Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened Wednesday to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz and other U.S. "investments" if the U.S. launches new strikes on Iranian infrastructure.
- Despite global oil prices remaining near five-month highs, President Trump insisted Tuesday that "we're doing very well" with Iran, adding that he was yet to "make a final decision of which way do we want to win" the war, "the nice way or the not nice way."
One killed, 8 injured in Dammam airport attack, Saudis say
An attack targeting the King Fahd International Airport in the eastern Saudi Arabian city of Dammam killed one person and injured eight others Wednesday evening, the kingdom's civil aviation authority said.
The authority said in a statement that injuries from the attack ranged from "minor to serious" and that material damage to the airport was also being assessed.
It did not describe what type of attack occurred, but the kingdom's airports have been targeted repeatedly by projectiles in recent days by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants.
U.S. troops reducing footprint at Middle East posts, sources say
A U.S. official and a senior U.S. military official told CBS News on Wednesday the military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing regional threats from the Houthis and direct threats from Iran.
NBC News was first to report on the drawdowns.
Asked about the reports, U.S. Central Command spokesperson Capt. Tim Hawkins told CBS News: "We regularly move U.S. service members and assets to optimize mission readiness. We do not discuss related movements for operational security reasons. U.S. forces remain vigilant and ready to protect American personnel and interests across the region."
The U.S. State Department has also ordered non-essential U.S. embassy personnel and their families to depart Saudi Arabia, citing threats posed by the Iran-backed Houthis.
CBS News has learned several U.S. embassies in the Middle East have adjusted their staffing under "restricted operations" status.
The restricted operations status, which the department introduced in August amid flare-ups in the war with Iran, allows embassies to reduce staffing and services without fully suspending operations.
Debris from intercepted drone kills 2 in Saudi Arabia, energy ministry says
The Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured two others on Wednesday.
"The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others," the ministry said in a statement. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at the Shaybah oil field near the UAE border.
State Department orders some U.S. government employees and family members to leave Saudi Arabia
The U.S. has ordered all non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia as the kingdom faces escalating attacks by Houthi militants.
"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a social media post Wednesday.
The order came a few days after the , Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting.
"The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them," Pigott added.
U.S. will suffer "even greater strategic failure" if it chooses war over diplomacy, Iranian FM says
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi issued a warning to the U.S. on Wednesday afternoon, saying it should choose diplomacy over returning to war.
"Iran is prepared to give diplomacy another chance if we see strong evidence of a sincere desire by US to build trust & reach a just solution," he wrote on X, sharing a link to an opinion piece in the Financial Times. "But if US chooses war over diplomacy, it'll certainly result in an even greater strategic failure."
Araghchi that Iran and the U.S. were still involved in indirect negotiations via mediators over the seven-day ceasefire proposal from September. The proposal was outright rejected by President Trump, but Araghchi said the U.S. was trying to add further clauses to the agreement.
U.S. sanctions Greek law firm for alleged involvement in Iranian "shadow fleet"
The U.S. Treasury announced new sanctions on the Panamanian-Greek law firm Karnakis and Karnakis for involvement in Iran's "shadow fleet" as part of its Operation Economic Outcast.
The U.S. accuses Karnakis and Karnakis of being indirectly involved in Iran's illicit shipping operations for years. A "shadow fleet" refers to oil tankers that hide their true ownership in order to evade sanctions.
"Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. "Iran's facilitators must make a choice: Either you are with us or against us. We know who you are, we know what you're doing, and we will continue to take action."
The Treasury also said it sanctioned Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents, including a fleet of cargo vessels that has directly taken part in Iran's "shadow fleet" and "helped generate substantial revenue for the Iranian regime."
Riyadh airport partially reopens after deadly Houthi strike
A limited number of Saudi airlines took off and landed at the country's main airport on Wednesday, two days after authorities notified airlines that they could resume operations with prior permission.
Saudia and FlyNas were operating flights Wednesday, according to flight-tracking data published by FlightAware. Major carriers, including Lufthansa and Air France, have canceled flights through mid-November.
Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has been hit multiple times this month by Yemen's Houthi rebels and shut down on Oct. 10. A strike two weeks ago killed 13 people and injured hundreds more.
The Houthis have acknowledged attacking the airport, claiming without evidence that Saudi Arabia provided military equipment to government forces through the facility.
Iran criticizes potential Egyptian involvement in Yemen war; Sisi promises only defensive actions
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation "more difficult."
"Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict," said Iran's top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday.
"We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult," Araghchi noted.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo's proposed military support for Riyadh was to "defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen," according to a statement from his office.
At a government event titled Egypt Forum 2026, Sisi said the "objective is to defend the kingdom's lands and borders, as well as those of any other Arab state, should it be requested of Egypt," his spokesman said in a statement.
Sisi on Saturday had asked parliament to authorize support for Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis, "if requested."
The parliament, which is stacked with supporters of the president, has since held two rare secret sessions, before postponing deliberations until next week.
Iran's new defense minister says first priority is meeting air force needs
Iran's newly appointed defense minister, Mehrdad Akhlaghi, said Wednesday his first hours in office were devoted to meeting the requirements of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Aerospace Force and the army's air defense units.
"We are not in a war of rhetoric in response to repeated threats; we are turning threats into greater readiness and more effective defensive power," he wrote in his first post on X since taking office.
Akhlaghi added Iran was concentrating on its objectives through the use of new technologies.
"We may eat dirt, but we will not give up our soil," he concluded.
Trump blocked Netanyahu's plan for multiday strikes on Iran, report says
President Trump blocked a planned Israeli multiday operation that would have resumed strikes against Iran on the weekend of Oct. 10, according to the Financial Times.
The plan was designed to exceed the intensity of the joint U.S.-Israeli military offensive launched in February, three people familiar with the matter told the paper, and would have struck Iranian nuclear sites, regime targets and civilian infrastructure such as power plants.
The president blocked the strike to avoid escalating conflict before the U.S. midterm elections, according to the report.
Iranian regime needs to be toppled, Netanyahu says
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday he had directed the Israeli army and intelligence services to topple the Iranian regime.

Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Flow Calibration Systems market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The World Flow Calibration Systems market is entering a structurally stronger demand phase as precision measurement becomes a binding constraint across semiconductor fabrication, pharmaceutical quality control, and industrial process automation. IndexBox projects the market to expand at a compound annual rate of 6–8% through 2035, with the growth trajectory supported by rising device complexity, tighter metrology tolerances, and the broader adoption of Industry 4.0 architectures that require traceable, digitally documented flow verification.
Semiconductor and precision manufacturing end-use segments collectively account for an estimated 30–38% of global demand, while industrial automation and instrumentation represent a further 25–33%, making electronics-adjacent industries the dominant consumption axis. Supply remains concentrated: fewer than 20 specialized manufacturers and OEM-integrated suppliers generate the majority of world revenue, and qualification cycles of 6–18 months create meaningful barriers for new entrants. Demand is shifting toward integrated calibration systems with digital connectivity, remote validation capabilities, and compliance-ready documentation.
Consumables and replacement parts now contribute an estimated 18–24% of annual market revenue, a share that is gradually rising as installed bases age and operators prioritize lifecycle cost management. Regulatory harmonization around ISO 17025 and sector-specific metrology requirements is accelerating cross-border procurement, particularly for OEMs and system integrators serving multiple geographies. At the same time, input cost volatility for precision components and export-controlled measurement technology introduce margin and compliance pressures that shape competitive positioning through the forecast period.
The baseline scenario for the World Flow Calibration Systems market assumes continued expansion at a 6–8% compound annual rate through 2035, with the market index rising from 100 in 2025 to a projected 185–210 by 2035. This outlook is anchored in three observable demand pillars. First, semiconductor and precision manufacturing capex remains on an upward path as device geometries shrink and new fabs come online, directly increasing the number of flow calibration points per production line.
Second, industrial automation and instrumentation spending is broadening beyond traditional process industries into electronics assembly, battery manufacturing, and specialty chemicals, where flow verification is embedded in quality management systems. Third, the installed base of calibration equipment is aging, and replacement and consumables demand is becoming a larger, more predictable revenue stream, now estimated at 18–24% of annual market revenue. On the supply side, concentration among fewer than 20 specialized manufacturers and OEM-integrated suppliers persists, and qualification cycles of 6–18 months limit rapid capacity expansion.
Input cost volatility for mass flow controllers, pressure sensors, and specialty metals has compressed gross margins by an estimated 3–6 percentage points since 2022 for manufacturers with limited pricing power, and export-controlled measurement technology adds compliance costs that can reach 10–20% of total project expenses for cross-border shipments. These constraints temper, but do not reverse, the growth trajectory. The baseline assumes no major regulatory disruption and a gradual easing of component cost pressures after 2027, with digital connectivity and remote validation capabilities becoming standard requirements in integrated systems by the early 2030s.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
- Rising precision requirements in semiconductor fabrication, where tighter flow tolerances and more calibration points per tool drive demand for integrated calibration systems
- Industrial process automation and Industry 4.0 adoption, supported by digital connectivity and remote validation capabilities that require traceable flow verification

- Aging installed base of calibration equipment, lifting consumables and replacement parts demand as operators prioritize lifecycle cost management
- Expansion of electronics and optical systems manufacturing, where flow calibration is embedded in quality management and process control
- Growth in OEM integration and maintenance contracts, as equipment builders bundle calibration systems with service agreements
Potential Growth Constraints
- Supplier qualification and documentation burdens extend procurement lead times by 8–16 weeks for first-time buyers, slowing deployment in fast-moving production environments
- Input cost volatility for precision components such as mass flow controllers, pressure sensors, and specialty metals has compressed gross margins by an estimated 3–6 percentage points since 2022
- Regulatory divergence and export controls on measurement technology used in semiconductor and aerospace applications add compliance costs of 10–20% to total project expenses
- High supply concentration among fewer than 20 specialized manufacturers limits competitive pricing and rapid capacity expansion
- Long qualification cycles of 6–18 months create barriers for new entrants and constrain the pace of technology substitution

Semiconductor and Precision Manufacturing (estimated share: 34%)
Semiconductor fabrication is the most demanding application for flow calibration systems because gas and liquid flow rates directly affect deposition uniformity, etch selectivity, and yield. Each new process node and each additional chamber adds calibration points, and the tolerance bands tighten with every generation. Through 2035, the shift toward advanced packaging, compound semiconductors, and 300mm wafer capacity in Asia-Pacific and North America will increase the installed base of mass flow controllers and the frequency of calibration verification. Demand-side indicators to watch include fab construction announcements, wafer starts per month, and the ratio of calibration systems to process tools.
The mechanism is straightforward: more process steps and tighter tolerances require more frequent verification, which raises both capital and consumables demand. Integrated calibration systems with digital documentation are becoming the default specification because fabs need audit-ready records for quality management. This segment is also the most sensitive to export controls, which can delay cross-border shipments of calibration equipment and add compliance costs. Major trends: Tighter flow tolerance requirements at advanced process nodes, Growth in compound semiconductor and advanced packaging capacity, Digital documentation and remote validation for audit readiness, Export controls affecting cross-border equipment shipments, and Rising calibration point density per process tool.

Industrial automation and instrumentation represents the broadest demand base for flow calibration systems, spanning chemical processing, oil and gas, power generation, water treatment, and food and beverage. The mechanism driving growth is the increasing embedding of flow measurement in closed-loop control and quality management systems, where an uncalibrated sensor can cascade into product quality deviations and compliance failures. Through 2035, the adoption of Industry 4.0 architectures will raise the number of connected measurement points and create demand for calibration systems that can validate remote sensors and generate digital records.
Demand-side indicators include industrial capex, automation penetration rates, and the number of connected instruments per plant. The segment is less cyclical than semiconductor capex but more sensitive to energy prices and maintenance budgets. articles.title: Cannondale is closing Connecticut offices, moving to California - Bicycle Retailer & Industry News
articles.summary: Cannondale is closing Connecticut offices, moving to California  Bicycle Retailer & Industry NewsCannondale's Wilton Office To Close, 143 Positions Affected  PatchCannondale Will Shut Down Connecticut Headquarters By Mid-2027, Laying Off 143 Workers  PinkbikeBicycle company to close CT office, layoffs to affect 143 workers  Hartford Business JournalCannondale will close its US headquarters  Escape Collective
articles.full_text:
WILTON, Conn. (BRAIN) — Cannondale is closing its longtime headquarters building here and consolidating its North American sales and operations in Santa Cruz, California. California is home to fellow Pon.Bike-owned brands Santa Cruz and Cervélo.
Cannondale's global headquarters will move from Connecticut to Woudenberg, Netherlands, which currently is Cannondale's European headquarters. Cannondale's global research and development and engineering functions will continue to be based in Freiburg, Germany.
The move was announced to Cannondale employees and dealers Wednesday morning. The closure will be final in mid-2027, with some workers staying with the company until the end of next year.
For dealers, the move means they will have a single point of contact for the Santa Cruz, Cervélo, and Cannondale bike brands as Cannondale will add outside sales reps who will cover the three brands.
"The aim is to make it easier for retailers to work with Cannondale and access more of the Pon.Bike portfolio. Each brand will retain its own identity, models and relationship with riders," the company said in a media statement.
The move will occur over the next six months as the brand closes its Wilton office.
Cannondale filed a notice with the Connecticut Department of Labor on Wednesday, notifying the department of the closure.
"The entire office will be closed and almost all employees there will be impacted," reads a letter to the department signed by Maggie Lansdale, global vice president of People for Cycling Sports Group, Cannondale's business unit within Pon. "The first separations are expected to occur on December 21, 2026, and separations are expected to continue in phases through December 31, 2027. The closure and separations will be permanent," the letter continues.
The letter includes a list of 143 workers who may be affected by the closure, including their titles, current work location and anticipated separation date. The dates range from December this year to the end of 2027. The list includes workers who work remotely, including some who are not based in Connecticut. The workers include about 14 account managers, all listed as remote workers, whose final day will be Feb. 28, 2027. The notice also said some of the 143 workers on the list are Pacific Cycle employees. Pacific Cycle, based is Madison, Wisconsin, is the Pon.bike business unit that handles the Schwinn, Mongoose, and Roadmaster brands.
History
Cannondale was founded in Wilton in 1971, taking its name from a train station in the town. The company later moved its headquarter to nearby Bethel, and later moved back to Wilton in 2013. Pon acquired Cannondale as part of its acquisition of Dorel Sports in 2022. The company last announced a workforce reduction in 2022.

articles.summary: What to know about GLP-1s and cannabis use  LiveNOW from FOXCompounded GLP-1 drugs recalled amid rising concerns over unapproved weight-loss alternatives  The Boston GlobeGLP-1 injections recalled nationwide over sterility concerns  Fox BusinessGLP-1 recall: Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised to second-highest level  MassLive.comGLP-1 injections recalled nationwide. See affected products  USA Today
articles.full_text:
Apothecary Pharma is recalling 23 vials of injectable drugs distributed nationwide because their sterility cannot be guaranteed, according to the Food and Drug Administration.
Dig deeper:
The voluntary recall includes 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication with the same active ingredient as Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound, as well as one vial of NAD+ injection. The FDA classified the recall as Class II on Oct. 8, meaning serious health problems are unlikely.
RELATED: Cheddar cheese recalled across several states over dangerous E. coli
The recall comes after the FDA sent Apothecary Pharma, a North Carolina company, a warning letter in December 2025 citing serious deficiencies in its sterile drug manufacturing practices. The agency said the issues posed risks to patients but has not linked those findings to the current recall.
The affected tirzepatide is an 18 mg/mL prescription injection packaged in a 4 mL multidose vial. Its NDC number is 85091-001-18. Recalled lots include AP-202622 through AP-202625 and AP-202627 through AP-202644, with beyond-use dates ranging from Oct. 7 to Nov. 26, 2026.
The recalled NAD+ injection is a 200 mg/mL prescription product packaged in a 6 mL multidose vial. Its NDC number is 85091-011-06. The affected lot is AP-202647, with a beyond-use date of Oct. 13, 2026.
Apothecary Pharma began the recall Sept. 24 and notified recipients by letter. The recall is ongoing.
What you can do:
Consumers should check their vials or pharmacy records, stop using any affected products and contact their pharmacist or prescriber for guidance. Anyone who experiences fever, redness, swelling or worsening pain after receiving an affected injection should seek medical attention.
The FDA notice did not report any illnesses or injuries associated with the recalled products.
The Source: FOX Business contributed to this report. The information in this story came from a recall notice issued by the Food and Drug Administration. This story was reported from Los Angeles.

articles.title: The Kremlin wants Russian media to call attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ‘Putin strikes.’ The inspiration? Stalin. - Meduza
articles.summary: The Kremlin wants Russian media to call attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ‘Putin strikes.’ The inspiration? Stalin.  MeduzaThis Could Be Ukraine's Worst Winter Yet - Persuasion  Persuasion | Yascha MounkRussia expands attacks on energy facilities to western Ukraine  ReutersPutin is carrying the war to Ukraine’s civilians. This is how to stop him  The TelegraphWhy Russia Sees a Window to Bomb Ukraine Into Submission This Winter  The New Y...
articles.full_text:
Russia’s Presidential Administration has ordered state and Kremlin-aligned media outlets to begin writing about “Putin strikes” on Ukraine, two employees at such outlets told Meduza.
The Presidential Administration’s political bloc sent loyalist media recommendations advising them to report that “the effectiveness and efficiency of Russia’s strikes far exceed what the Ukrainian military has achieved.”
“Our ballistic weapons have performed flawlessly. The Ukrainian regime has lost its most important production and storage sites, where cruise missiles and drones, along with their components, were assembled and stored. ‘Putin strikes’ are far larger in scale and more effective than enemy attacks. We are shutting down the militants’ missile programs, which helps keep Russia’s regions secure,” the guidance document says.
Headlines, comments from servicemen, and articles using the phrase “Putin strikes” indeed appeared this week in major Russian media outlets.
For example, the Russian news website Gazeta.ru published an article with the following subheadline:
“SVO” veteran Konovalov: “Putin strikes” deprive the Ukrainian military of the ability to fight.
The outlet cites Vitaly Konovalov, head of the Association of Veterans of the Russia-Ukraine War in Stavropol Krai, who says the strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure are allegedly aimed at undermining supplies to the Ukrainian military. Notably, Konovalov himself never uses the phrase “Putin strikes.” It appears in the connecting phrases and generalizations added by propagandists.
Novye Izvestia published an article titled “Putin Strikes on Ukraine: Ukrainian Military Left Without Electricity and Weapons.” Rosbalt used the phrase in the headline of a news item titled “Putin Strikes on Ukraine: Ukrainian Military Losing Logistics Hubs, Substations, and Vessels.” It also appears in headlines and articles from Fedpress. Segodnia.ru writes about a “series of “Putin strikes.”” The phrase has even appeared in pro-government Instagram accounts.
A political consultant who works with the Presidential Administration’s political bloc said directly linking Putin to the strikes on Ukraine is meant to try to boost the president’s approval ratings.
According to polls by the Public Opinion Foundation (FOM), Putin’s approval rating fell from 75% in July to 71% in early October, while trust in him fell from 74% to 70% over the same period.
“In this case, [the idea is to raise the ratings] among the pro-war, ultra-patriotic segment of society, who need to be shown some successes from the war. To the question “What has been accomplished?” [at the front], the suggested answer is “Putin strikes,” by analogy with the “Stalinist strikes,”” the consultant said.
During Joseph Stalin’s rule, the term “Ten Stalinist Strikes” referred to 10 major Soviet army operations during World War II.
The source told Meduza that it is hard to assess how effective the appearance of “Putin strikes” in the press has been: “Maybe it will have some effect on the older segment [of society].”
Speaking at a press conference in Bishkek on September 1, following the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit, Vladimir Putin said he had ordered the Russian military to prepare and carry out massive strikes on Ukraine’s energy facilities. “They’re striking our people, so they’ll get a response,” he added.
In mid-October, discussing the Russian army’s strikes on Ukraine, Putin said:
They took the first step. We started responding. Now they’re whining about energy facilities too, and about other targets, including data centers and so on. They started it. They shouldn’t have started it.

articles.full_text:
Kazakhstan and Thailand Strengthen Trade, Economic and Investment Partnership
Images | AI
On the occasion of the Republic Day of Kazakhstan, the Embassy of the Republic of Kazakhstan in the Kingdom of Thailand organised the business conference "Kazakhstan-Thailand: Towards a Comprehensive Partnership."
The event brought together representatives of government agencies, business associations and companies from both countries. Welcoming remarks were delivered by Ambassador of Kazakhstan to Thailand Margulan Baimukhan, Thailand Trade Representative Werapong Prapha, Vice Minister for Commerce of Thailand Kirida Bhaopichitr, and Vice Chairman of the Thai Chamber of Commerce Visit Limlurcha.
Thailand Trade Representative Werapong Prapha, in turn, stressed that Kazakhstan and Thailand have significant opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation and are well positioned to serve as strategic gateways connecting Central Asia and Europe with Southeast Asia and the Asia-Pacific region. He expressed confidence that closer cooperation between the business communities of the two countries would open new avenues for economic engagement and further advance bilateral trade.
Speaking at the opening of the conference, Thailand's Vice Minister for Commerce Dr. Kirida Bhaopichitr congratulated the people of Kazakhstan on the forthcoming Republic Day. She highlighted the special significance of the upcoming 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations, noting the complementarity of the two economies and the considerable potential for expanding cooperation in trade and investment.
Vice Chairman of the Thai Chamber of Commerce Visit Limlurcha reaffirmed the Thai business community’s interest in developing trade and investment cooperation with Kazakhstan and expanding direct ties between the business communities of the two countries.
Margulan Baimukhan highlighted the positive dynamics of bilateral economic relations. In 2025, trade turnover between Kazakhstan and Thailand increased by 8% to approximately USD 255 million. During the first eight months of 2026, bilateral trade reached USD 182.3 million, representing an increase of 14.3%.
The Kazakh diplomat emphasised the importance of moving beyond traditional trade towards mutual investment, joint production, technology transfer and long-term business partnerships.
During the presentation, the Kazakh side outlined the country’s economic and investment potential, transit and logistics capabilities, as well as measures available to support foreign investors. Promising areas of cooperation included agriculture and food processing, critical minerals, energy, industry, transport and logistics, digital technologies, artificial intelligence, tourism and hospitality.
Kazakhstan invited Thai companies to use the country as a manufacturing and logistics platform for accessing the markets of Central Asia and Eurasia. Particular attention was given to opportunities for combining Kazakhstan’s resources and infrastructure with Thailand’s technological, manufacturing and managerial expertise.

articles.title: U.K. inflation rise to highest in almost a year as Iran war drives fuel prices higher - The Tribune-Democrat
articles.summary: U.K. inflation rise to highest in almost a year as Iran war drives fuel prices higher  The Tribune-Democrat
articles.full_text:
LONDON – Inflation in the U.K. rose to its highest rate in almost a year as the Iran war continues to ratchet up fuel prices, official figures showed Wednesday, cementing market expectations that the Bank of England will raise interest rates next month.
The Office for National Statistics said consumer prices rose by 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1% in August. That's the highest reading since October last year, and above the 3.4% that most economists had been expecting for the month.
The increase takes inflation further above the Bank of England's target rate of 2%.
Prices across the transport industry were the biggest contributor to higher inflation last month, particularly at the pump. Overall, motor fuels soared by 30% in the year to September, up from a 23% annual rise in August.
Fuel costs have been soaring because of the Iran war and the ensuing bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz, which have squeezed global oil and gas supplies.
Treasury chief John Healey said his budget statement next week will aim to give businesses and families “some breathing space” from the upward march in the cost of living.
Whatever measures he comes up with to keep a lid on rising prices, economists expect the Bank of England to increase interest rates at its next meeting on Nov. 5. Last month, rate-setters held the bank's main rate at 3.75% but gave a big hint that they were ready to hike soon.
“With inflation increasing, the pieces are falling firmly into place for a November rate rise," said Suren Thiru, chief economist at ICAEW.
Most economists expect an increase in the bank's main rate to 4%. Other central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, have raised rates recently.
Interest rates in the U.K. had been trending downward from a 15-year high of 5.25% until the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
