articles.title: Attracting high-tech investment: Lessons from India for Vietnam - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Attracting high-tech investment: Lessons from India for Vietnam  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Backed by billions of dollars in subsidies, India's high-tech manufacturing sector is steadily integrating into global supply chains, but still faces challenges related to added value and investment efficiency.
This experience highlights the requirements for Vietnam in implementing Resolution 57: attracting investment must go hand in hand with enhancing endogenous technological capacity and mastering high-value-added stages.
Optimists argue that Apple's move to shift some iPhone production to India helps the country reduce its dependence on China and improve its position in the global supply chain. Currently, about a quarter of iPhones are manufactured in factories near Chennai, providing jobs for tens of thousands of workers.
However, skeptics argue that much of the activity remains focused on final assembly, which creates little added value. Nevertheless, Indian factories have begun taking on more stages, from assembling components onto circuit boards to manufacturing motherboards.
The core question is whether these advances are commensurate with the state subsidies. If competitiveness cannot be maintained without budgetary support, the gains of India's manufacturing sector risk reversing.
Moving deeper into the global supply chain.
Smartphones use many high-value components such as circuit boards, camera modules, and screens. To truly improve its position in the production chain, the export value of finished phones needs to increase faster than the import of input components.
However, the evaluation is not simple because many imported components are also used in electric vehicles , solar panels, and other equipment.
In 2023, former Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan and two colleagues developed three scenarios, assuming that 40%, 60%, or 80% of imported components in the multipurpose category were used in mobile phones. In all three cases, India's mobile phone trade balance remained in deficit. The research team argued that the increase in finished phone exports was not enough to demonstrate that the country's manufacturing capacity had reached a breakthrough.
Newer analysis shows that the trade balance remains in deficit, but the gap between component imports and phone exports has narrowed. This indicates progress in domestic manufacturing, although it is not yet possible to say that India has mastered the majority of the product's value.
Value added remains limited.
You may also like
Indian suppliers have expanded into more complex processes, but the lack of mastery in the production of memory chips, processors, lenses, displays, and batteries still limits the ability to create domestic value.
With the iPhone 14, India narrowed the production gap with China to just two months, up from six to nine months previously. The iPhone 15 was the first model Apple manufactured in India to be ready for the global launch from day one.
Suppliers, including Foxconn, have also shifted from importing complete circuit boards to assembling components directly in India. Motherboard manufacturing alone is expected to improve the trade balance by $2.1 billion in the 2025-2026 fiscal year.
However, the outlook remains uncertain. Strong demand for memory chips from data centers is driving up the price of semiconductors used in phones. Meanwhile, demand for phones in the Indian market is declining, especially in the low-cost segment. This could reduce component imports, but weaker global smartphone sales also risk impacting exports.
Subsidies are putting increasing pressure on the budget.
Five years ago, India implemented a subsidy program equivalent to 4-6% of the finished phone bill value to offset infrastructure disadvantages and production costs. As chip prices rise due to demand from the artificial intelligence (AI) sector, the budget may have to bear additional support costs.
With a subsidy rate of 4%, for every additional $1 billion in the bill value solely due to rising chip prices, the budget would have to spend an extra $40 million. Thus, even if production doesn't increase proportionally, the cost of subsidies could still balloon.
To move further into the supply chain, the Indian government has allocated an additional $13.4 billion to develop the domestic semiconductor industry. However, the $10 billion subsidy introduced five years ago has mainly helped establish overseas chip packaging facilities, failing to create advanced chip manufacturing capabilities.
Advanced chip manufacturing requires cutting-edge technology, significant capital investment, and the ability to accept long periods without profitability. India still faces challenges in all three areas. Even Tata Group, a key Apple partner in the country and the company behind India's only semiconductor manufacturing plant project, is facing disputes over control and concerns related to the scale of investment in the electronics sector.
International experience shows that moving up to higher-tech stages is not easy. Malaysia developed chip packaging and circuit board assembly operations from the 1970s, but its progress up the value chain stalled after the country reached upper-middle income status in 1992. Meanwhile, South Korea and Taiwan (China) leveraged the semiconductor industry to rise to the ranks of wealthy economies.
It's not easy to copy the Chinese model.
India can hardly rely solely on billions of dollars in investment to quickly catch up with the world's leading high-tech manufacturing hubs. Instead, it needs to develop its design and engineering capabilities while allocating resources to healthcare, education, climate change response, and labor-intensive industries such as textiles, footwear, and toys.
You may also like
The Chinese model is particularly difficult to replicate. Apple's success in the country is linked to Foxconn's ability to coordinate with local authorities to rapidly build large-scale factory complexes. This combination of deployment speed, production scale, and risk tolerance is an advantage that India will find difficult to replicate.
Apple may be able to help India improve its manufacturing capabilities and become more deeply involved in the global supply chain, but that doesn't mean the country will become the next factory of the world. Continuing to increase subsidies in the hope of replicating the Chinese model could lead to ever-increasing costs without necessarily delivering commensurate benefits.
From attracting investment to mastering technology: Lessons for Vietnam
Drawing lessons from India's experience, Vietnam can develop high-tech industries in line with the spirit of Resolution 57-NQ/TW dated December 22, 2024, of the Politburo on breakthroughs in national science, technology, innovation, and digital transformation. Investment incentives may attract large corporations, but they cannot replace endogenous technological capabilities and the ability to master high value-added processes.
Therefore, support policies need to be linked to tangible results such as technology transfer, development of supporting industries, training of high-quality human resources, and enhancement of research, design, and manufacturing capabilities. Regular evaluation of budget utilization efficiency is also essential to limit prolonged reliance on incentives without building sustainable competitiveness.
More importantly, Vietnam needs to focus on investing in research and development, digital infrastructure, education, and linkages between businesses and research institutions. This is the foundation for science, technology, and innovation to truly become a driving force for productivity enhancement, helping domestic businesses move up to higher value-added stages in the global supply chain, instead of primarily relying on processing and assembly.

articles.title: An Independent Canada Struggles with Energy-Fueled Inflation - Industrial Info
articles.summary: An Independent Canada Struggles with Energy-Fueled Inflation  Industrial Info
articles.full_text:
Pipelines
An Independent Canada Struggles with Energy-Fueled Inflation
A 'no' vote on an independence referendum means Alberta remains the hub of Canada's energy sector for the foreseeable future.
Released Wednesday, October 21, 2026
Written by Daniel Graeber for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas)
Summary
Federal data from Canada show annual inflation to September was up 3.1%, driven primarily by a geopolitical risk premium supporting commodity prices. After a failed referendum on an independent Alberta, the country is moving forward with a unified stance.
Albertans Choose to Stay
While collectively facing pressure from higher commodity prices, Canadians woke up Tuesday to a unified nation after a referendum charting a path to an independent Alberta failed.
"On October 19, Albertans made a clear choice. They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other," Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement Tuesday. "Above all, Albertans chose Canada."
Industrial Info Resources offered a deep dive into the energy impacts of an independent Alberta. For instance, the fate of the Trans Mountain crude oil pipeline, co-owned by the federal government but originating in Alberta, would be unclear. It's the only pipeline in Canada that can deliver oil outside of North America.
A study from the University of Calgary, meanwhile, found the United States would likely exploit an independent Alberta given the already-strong economic ties. Alberta is home to most of the Canadian crude oil production, and much of that winds up as exports to the United States.
Federal U.S. data show Canada delivered 3.7 million barrels per day (bpd) to the United States over the week ending Oct. 9, accounting for 63% of the total. Industrial Info Resources, meanwhile, finds a vast network of just crude oil pipelines emanating from a province that sits on some of the largest oil deposits in the world.
The Canadian benchmark for crude oil, Western Canadian Select, usually trades at a discount to rival benchmarks such as West Texas Intermediate in the United States. Compared to the light-sweet oil found in U.S. shale deposits, most of the Canadian oil is heavy-sour. It's harder to refine, churns out fewer valuable end-products and is largely isolated to North America, all factors that help explain the discount.
Early Tuesday, the front-month contract for West Texas Intermediate was trading at around $100 per barrel, while Western Canadian Select was at $86.19.
Industrial Info is tracking 18 operational refineries in the Canadian energy sector with a combined 1.95 million bpd of capacity. Imperial Oil, majority owned by U.S. supermajor ExxonMobil, leads the pack in terms of operational capacity.
Inflation Would Only be 2.2% if Not for Energy
A well-functioning downstream sector and a discounted benchmark, however, aren't enough to tame inflation. Under pressure from U.S. military endeavors in the Middle East, global commodity prices have been supported by a geopolitical risk premium since the conflict began in late February.
"Crude oil prices increased in September, reaching their highest level since May amid ongoing uncertainty about the wars in the Middle East, resulting in higher prices for gasoline and fuel oil," the federal Canadian government said.
The Consumer Price Index in Canada increased 3.1% on an annual basis to September. Stripping out the impact of energy and consumer-level inflation was closer to 2.2%. Gasoline prices alone were up nearly 30% annually to September.
The inflationary pressures come as Prime Minister Carney works to advance an economic agenda that draws on trade diversity given the pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump. Since taking office last year, Carney established an office that will fast-track projects of national interest.
"We are building that future, bigger and faster than ever before," he said Monday. "Canada is securing new trade partners around the world, fast-tracking major, nation-building projects in every part of the country, and unleashing our full potential as a global energy superpower with Alberta at its core."
Alberta will serve as the starting point for a new crude oil pipeline dubbed Pacific Link, recently designated as a project of interest. Included in a joint agreement between Alberta and the federal government earlier this year, data from Industrial Info Resources show the line could carry as much as 1 million bpd.
The first phase of the project could begin next year. It would add to the nation's export potential by tapping Asian economies, with the provincial government of Alberta estimating it could draw in as much as US$140 billion in direct investments for Canada and increase gross domestic product by more than US$20 billion.
By the Numbers
- 30% y-o-y spike in Canadian retail gasoline prices
- $14 discount to WTI for Western Canadian Select
Key Takeaways
- Albertans on Monday rejected a referendum that would have led to independence.
- Prime Minister Carney said he needs Alberta as a component of a comprehensive trade strategy.

articles.title: Korea’s exports near $1 trillion milestone, but US trade risks cloud outlook - 한겨레
articles.summary: Korea’s exports near $1 trillion milestone, but US trade risks cloud outlook  한겨레
articles.full_text:
Representatives of around 90 South Korean export companies attend a briefing on addressing non-tariff barriers to diversify export markets at the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) in Seoul’s Seocho District on Oct. 20, 2026. (courtesy MOTIR)
          Korea’s exports in the first nine months of the year hit US$814.72 billion in value, according to data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA). With the economy breaking export records every month this year, the milestone of US$1 trillion for the year is expected to be reached around Nov. 20. 
Hitting this mark would make Korea only the fourth country in the world to do so, behind the US, China and Germany.
Excluding the Netherlands and Hong Kong, both of which have a high volume of re-exports since they are gateway ports for landlocked countries, Korea has surpassed Japan as the world’s No. 4 exporter.
But uncertainty in Korea is growing over export and investment conditions. Discussions of the US — Korea’s second-largest export market worth US$151.8 billion as of last month and a core strategic ally in national security, economy and advanced technology — are increasingly seeing the use of terms such as “risk,” “dispute” and “response.”
Up until now, these expressions were most frequently used to describe not the US, but China, Korea’s top export destination as of last month, worth US$171.5 billion.
But recent reports — such as those from KITA (“Intensifying US Efforts to Contain China through Reciprocal Trade Agreements and Corporate Responses”); the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (“A Study on Investor-State Disputes Related to Investment in the US”); Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry (“Briefing on Managing US Trade Risks for Exporters”); and the National Assembly Research Service (“Expanding Scope of US Tariff Policy Assessments and Trade-related Risks with Domestic Legislation”), and more — reflect the anxiety and fear felt by businesses and the market as the US increasingly sidelines decades-old multilateral trade rules in pursuit of its own interests.
A seminar on Monday on responding to investment risks in the US was hosted by the Korean Commercial Arbitration Board, the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the Korean Society of International Economic Law. Attended by trade experts and representatives from export and investment companies, the event focused on topics like “risks in the US market,” “protecting the rights of Korean companies” and “responding to disputes.”
“Shifts in US trade and industrial policies, especially those on tariffs and supply chains, are creating new uncertainty and challenges for Korean companies,” said Shin Hyun-yoon, the president of the Korean Commercial Arbitration Board.
The speakers covered a range of topics, from practical issues like drafting contracts that cover abrupt changes in tariffs to systemic issues like shifts in US trade policy leveraging Section 301 of the Trade Act and Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act.
Chung Ki-chang, a senior foreign attorney at Lee & Ko, highlighted the difficulty in responding to the situation. “The US is blatantly violating World Trade Organization agreements, but it’s ultimately still the country with the capacity to buy our key exports such as semiconductors and ships,” he said. 
Kim Se-jin, a senior foreign attorney at Shin & Kim, noted, “The US is demanding ‘no-China’ contracts to exclude China from supply chains, but meeting this requirement is difficult in practice and could fuel contractual disputes. In the end, this could expose Korean companies to a ‘no-China risk.’”
The CEO of a startup questioned whether the US market was still a safe bet, given the growing rift between Washington and Canada, once close allies.
A question from the audience, tinged with a bit of hope, asked about the possibility of a change in US trade policy after the Trump administration leaves office.
Jahng Jeong-ju, a partner at law firm Hwawoo, cautioned that while tariffs may be a powerful tool for pressuring companies to invest in the US, their long-term effectiveness remains questionable. 
With the US trade deficit widening again, he said, the policy may struggle to deliver lasting results — yet businesses should not expect a major shift in Washington’s approach after Trump leaves office. 
“Companies should bear in mind that the resolution of the tariff issue is unlikely in the near term,” he said.
Han Chang-wan, a partner at Bae, Kim & Lee LLC, noted that it was “impossible to predict” changes in US tariffs. 
“Contracts must include provisions such as a cap on tariff liabilities, renegotiation stipulations or a termination clause if negotiations fail,” he said. 
The National Assembly on Tuesday also discussed how to recoup the principal of the country’s investment pledge of US$350 billion in the US. An audit by the Finance and Economy Planning Committee saw bipartisan discussions on recovering US$200 billion in investment and US$150 billion in funds for bilateral shipbuilding cooperation as agreed in tariff talks with Washington.
Rep. Jung Sung-ho of the ruling Democratic Party said, “If not for President Trump’s unconventional tariff policies, investments like this probably would’ve never materialized. Improper risk management could wipe out our US$350 billion.”
By Kim Nam-il, staff reporter

articles.title: India’s $100 billion European Free Trade Association cheque is slow to clear as Vietnam joins the club - The Economic Times
articles.summary: India’s $100 billion European Free Trade Association cheque is slow to clear as Vietnam joins the club  The Economic Times
articles.full_text:
Listen to this article in summarized format
EFTA comprises Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, which are not EU members. The agreement was signed in Hanoi by senior representatives of the four EFTA states, including Swiss President Guy Parmelin, and by Vietnam's Minister of Industry and Trade Le Manh Hung, according to an EFTA document. Its entry into force is pending, the document said.
Also read: Vietnam's export boom offers India six lessons for growth
Bilateral trade between EFTA and Vietnam was EUR 4.8 billion in 2025, with a surplus of EUR 2.5 billion in Vietnam's favour, up from EUR 0.5 billion a decade earlier, according to EFTA. Electrical machinery, footwear and apparel, and mechanical machinery were the top imports from Vietnam.
India's Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) with EFTA was signed on March 10, 2024, and came into force on October 1, 2025. EFTA offered market access on 92.2% of its tariff lines, covering 99.6% of India's exports. India opened 82.7% of its tariff lines, covering 95.3% of EFTA's exports, according to the Press Information Bureau (PIB).
Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), said the deal will not affect India's exports. "EFTA countries levy zero tariffs on industrial products, so deal with Vietnam or any other country including India offers no additional tariff advantage in these markets," he said. Competition will depend on product quality, price and delivery reliability, he said.
Normal route or FTA route
EFTA's free trade dashboard says Iceland and Norway abolished tariffs on most industrial imports on their own, and Switzerland and Liechtenstein did so from January 1, 2024.
Preferences under an FTA are not automatic, the dashboard says. Importers must claim them, and goods must meet the agreement's rules of origin. It calculates preference utilisation only on the subset of trade where a preferential margin exists. Its data covers 2018 to 2024, before India's pact took effect.
India's exports to EFTA
Dhar said Vietnam's duty-free access to EFTA countries poses a significant challenge to India's ambition of increasing its presence there. He said Indian exporters have struggled to use the market access opportunities since the agreement was signed. Exports fell nearly 11% in 2025-26 and by over 9% in January to July 2026 over 2025, he said.
The Commerce Ministry said in May that India's exports to Switzerland, its largest EFTA partner, crossed $1.2 billion in 2025-26.
Products that overlap
India's exports to EFTA in 2024-25 included engineering goods worth $315 million, up 18% from the year before, according to the PIB. Dhar said telephones and electronics products, and textiles and clothing, have been among Vietnam's major exports to EFTA in recent years, and that India has considerable competitive strengths in these industries.
The European Union angle
EU-Vietnam goods trade was EUR 76 billion in 2025, and the EU's deficit was EUR 51.7 billion, according to the Commission. Machinery and appliances made up more than half of EU imports from Vietnam, followed by footwear and textiles.
On September 11, the Commission sent proposals to the EU Council seeking authorisation to sign and conclude the India deal.
India's Commerce Ministry put India's goods exports to the EU at $75.85 billion in 2024-25. It said $33 billion of India's labour-intensive exports, including textiles and leather and footwear, face EU duties of 4% to 26% and will move to zero at entry into force. It valued India's textile and apparel exports to the EU at $7.2 billion.
The $100 billion investment goal
Under Article 7.1(3) of TEPA, the EFTA states "shall aim to increase" foreign direct investment into India by $50 billion within 10 years of the agreement taking effect, and by another $50 billion in the following five years, according to the agreement text.
Also read: Vietnam's export triumph: How a small nation beat China and India to become America's top trade partner
The PIB describes the commitments as binding. Under Article 7.7, a sub-committee will review progress at five, 10 and 15 years. If the objectives are not met by the final review, India can seek consultations and, if they fail, take temporary measures to rebalance its tariff concessions, the text says.
Srivastava described the commitment as "just an aspirational target tied to India's high GDP growth and high returns to EFTA companies in India." Dhar said: "These are still early days to assess whether there has been any forward movement on this promise."
Data from the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) show cumulative FDI equity inflow from Switzerland, the largest EFTA source of investment in India, at $11.32 billion from April 2000 to March 2026. It was $10.88 billion up to June 2025, a rise of about $440 million.

articles.title: Southeast Asia Should Double Down on the AI Supply Chain - fulcrum.sg
articles.summary: Southeast Asia Should Double Down on the AI Supply Chain  fulcrum.sg
articles.full_text:
Southeast Asia Should Double Down on the AI Supply Chain
Published
AI-related exports are a bright spot in an otherwise gloomy global economy. This represents an opportunity for Southeast Asia.
Exports are booming in Asia. Strong growth in AI-related exports — the physical products needed for the global data centre buildout — is driving broader growth in the region. This surging demand is already offsetting the negative impacts from chaotic US trade policy and the Iran war. In fact, the demand is pushing AI supply chains to their limits; production capacity needs to expand. This is an opportunity for Southeast Asia to double down on export-led growth.
While frontier AI capabilities are largely being developed in the US and China, much of the AI infrastructure is being built in, and then exported from Asia. Global data centre capacity — the physical backbone of AI — is set to increase by a compound annual growth rate of 24.6 per cent between 2025 and 2027. Estimates suggest it could potentially double by 2030, creating an additional USD1–2 trillion in IT equipment purchases. In response, orders have risen sharply across semiconductor and electronics supply chains in Asia. AI-related trade is expanding at a much faster rate than trade in other products.
Japan, South Korea and Taiwan produce the most valuable and complex inputs and products along the AI supply chain, such as the most advanced semiconductors. Current capacity is already hitting physical bottlenecks, pushing up prices as demand outpaces supply. Some types of these chips are now five times more expensive, while memory component costs are up 300 per cent this year. The broader suite of less complex but still essential AI supply chain products such as central processing units are also facing production capacity constraints.
Southeast Asia has benefited from AI-related demand by providing less advanced inputs and participating in the assembly, testing and packaging (ATP) stage of the semiconductor supply chain. Some economies — Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam — already enjoy a comparative advantage in chip exports. New Lowy Institute research indicates global semiconductor supply chains are a promising growth opportunity. Southeast Asia is well positioned to continue moving into higher value-added activities.
As AI infrastructure demand outpaces the supply Asia can provide, Southeast Asia will be key for developing new capacity, especially for less advanced electronics manufacturing and semiconductor ATP. An Asian Development Bank report suggests exports of AI-related goods are the main channel developing countries in the Asia-Pacific can benefit from the AI boom. This stems from a boost to industrial output and employment.
As AI infrastructure demand outpaces the supply Asia can provide, Southeast Asia will be key for developing new capacity, especially for less advanced electronics manufacturing and semiconductor assembly, testing and packaging.
However, there are some risks to consider.
The Iran war has revealed that Southeast Asia’s industrial production networks are more exposed to an oil shock than those in China, which is the region’s key competitor in comparable AI-related exports. Accelerating the clean energy transition would help to reduce the region’s dependence on imported fossil fuels, building the economic resilience needed to remain competitive and shield its manufacturing sector from external shocks more effectively.
Semiconductor exports from the region are also facing headwinds. China continues to reduce imports as it builds a fully indigenous semiconductor ecosystem. Imports declined by over 20 per cent between 2021 and 2024. Deepening regional integration across the semiconductor supply chain would help offset declining Chinese demand by increasing economies of scale, thereby reducing unit costs and allowing greater specialisation. Deeper integration could also increase Southeast Asia’s consumption of its own exports.
Much has been written about whether AI investments are a bubble waiting to bring the global economy crashing down. There are good reasons to be sceptical of this view. Experts tend to agree that AI will be economically transformative, albeit with mixed views on the overall impacts on inequality and labour markets. Therefore, it is hard to imagine a future where large increases in production capacity across AI-related products are not needed, even with cyclical dynamics accounted for. Data centres require products across the semiconductor supply chain and other electronic inputs.This demand is unlikely to weaken in the long term as AI diffuses through the global economy. As such, Southeast Asia would need to increase its production capacity.
To better shield the broader economy from any downside risks, the private sector should be the primary driver of supply chain expansions. Governments have an essential role. They can crowd in multinational firms through favourable business environments, support skills development, provide common-use and specialised public infrastructure, and, where necessary, provide some policy support. However, reports that semiconductor firms engage in “incentive shopping”, extracting the most favourable tax and subsidy terms when establishing new projects is concerning. Governments would be remiss to commit substantial public financing for such projects considering current market dynamics. Unmet demand is likely sufficient to drive production expansions without major public financing.
Greater regional coordination, such as adopting an ASEAN ‘best practice’ investment facilitation mechanism, could also rationalise efforts to expand a regional AI-supply chain while further reducing the fiscal burden of attracting foreign investment. Improving regulatory conditions and transparency would help build long-term investor confidence and simultaneously uplift capabilities in lower-income economies. That would allow a more efficient allocation of foreign capital by encouraging lower value-add activities to migrate towards lower-cost economies like Cambodia and Vietnam. That would reduce the subsidy required to attract foreign investment in these economies while simultaneously freeing up input, construction, and fiscal capacity in more advanced economies like Malaysia and Singapore to support only higher-value activities.
Southeast Asian economies are already notable AI supply chain participants. The global AI boom is a strong signal that countries already reaping the benefits, such as Malaysia and Vietnam, should double down. Those less exposed to this boom like Indonesia and Cambodia should get on board quickly.
2026/291
Robert Walker is a Research Fellow at the Lowy Institute and works as an economist in the Institute’s Indo-Pacific Development Centre. His work focuses on growth and development in the Indo-Pacific region, emerging Asian economies, and strategic economic competition.

articles.title: Businesses need to prepare to seize opportunities from the Vietnam-EFTA Free Trade Agreement. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Businesses need to prepare to seize opportunities from the Vietnam-EFTA Free Trade Agreement.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
|  | 
| Businesses need to control quality, ensure transparency in the supply chain, and comply with rules of origin for goods exported to the EFTA region. | 
 Businesses need to "act" now.
 After 14 years of negotiations, Vietnam and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) signed the Vietnam-EFTA Free Trade Agreement (VEFTA) on October 18th. The agreement is currently awaiting ratification by member countries before it takes effect.
 EFTA is an intergovernmental organization promoting free trade and economic integration, currently comprising four members: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway , and Switzerland.
 According to data provided by EFTA, bilateral trade between Vietnam and the bloc is projected to reach €4.8 billion in 2025, with Vietnam having a trade surplus of €2.5 billion. This result demonstrates that the trade relationship between the two sides has a solid foundation and opens up opportunities for businesses to further expand their markets.
 Leaders of the Ministry of Industry and Trade believe that cooperation with EFTA partners can help Vietnamese businesses enhance their competitiveness, gradually meet higher international standards, and participate more deeply in global value chains.
 As the 18th FTA signed by Vietnam, VEFTA opens up more opportunities to access the European market, but to turn these opportunities into actual orders, businesses need to proactively prepare early, instead of waiting for the agreement to officially come into effect.
 For exports, one of the key requirements is meeting the rules of origin to qualify for preferential tariffs under the agreements. Proper preparation of raw materials, documentation proving origin, and appropriate management processes will help businesses take advantage of these benefits and improve their competitiveness against goods from other exporting countries.
 VEFTA covers many areas, including trade in goods, tariffs, technical barriers, customs, trade defense, services, investment, intellectual property, dispute resolution, trade, and sustainable development. Therefore, the impact of the agreement lies not only in reducing import tariffs but also in its ability to promote investment cooperation, technology transfer, and improve governance capacity.
 Norwegian Ambassador to Vietnam Stein Iversen believes that the agreement will create more opportunities for Vietnamese goods to access the EFTA market, while also giving consumers on both sides more product choices.
 According to the Ambassador, the fact that Norwegian seafood products have access to the Vietnamese market with favorable tariffs is of significant importance to bilateral trade. Conversely, Vietnamese goods also have more opportunities to compete in EFTA markets.
 He recommended that Vietnamese exporters and manufacturers carefully study the agreement's content, proactively identify opportunities that match their products and capabilities, and take advantage of them as soon as the commitments are implemented.
 Opportunities go hand in hand with improving product quality.
 While the Vietnam-EU Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA) opens up opportunities to access a market of over 450 million people, and the CPTPP connects Vietnam with a vast economic space in the Asia-Pacific region and other continents, the VEFTA expands Vietnam's presence in markets with high purchasing power and stringent standards.
 EFTA has a population of approximately 15 million people, a relatively small size compared to the EU or CPTPP. However, the bloc's attractiveness lies in its high income levels and demand for high-quality products. This presents opportunities for Vietnamese industries with competitive advantages such as agricultural products, seafood, textiles, footwear, wood products, and electronics.
 In return, EFTA markets impose strict requirements on quality, food safety, environmental protection, and social responsibility. Businesses wishing to expand exports not only need to meet market access conditions but also ensure the stability and transparency of the entire supply chain.
 Swiss Ambassador to Vietnam Thomas Gass noted that consumers in Switzerland and EFTA countries are increasingly interested in product sustainability. Factors such as working conditions, water reuse, recycling efficiency, waste control, and reducing plastic waste in the environment are all considered important.
 According to the Ambassador, products that meet these requirements well can gain an advantage in the market, because consumers are willing to pay more for goods produced sustainably.
 Conversely, Vietnam has a market of over 100 million people, a strategic location in the Asia-Pacific region, and a wide network of FTAs. This is an advantage for Vietnam to become an investment and production destination, and a gateway for EFTA businesses to expand their operations in ASEAN and other regional markets.
 For the seafood industry, according to the Vietnam Association of Seafood Processing and Export (Vasep), the agreement should be seen as an opportunity to access additional markets with high purchasing power and quality requirements, aligning with the orientation of increasing export value rather than just chasing production volume.
 A representative from Vasep stated that VEFTA is a significant step forward for the seafood industry, but the benefits from the agreement do not automatically translate into business advantages. Opportunities will belong to businesses that are well-prepared in terms of quality, certification, traceability, rules of origin, packaging, labeling, and the ability to meet the requirements of importers, retail systems, and food service providers in Switzerland, Norway, and Iceland.
 "While awaiting the ratification of the agreement, businesses need to review their product portfolios, study tariff commitments and rules of origin, assess the technical requirements of each market, and complete certification documents and traceability systems," Vasep noted.

articles.title: Australian lawmaker loses both legs in vehicle attack as suspect appears in court - NBC News
articles.summary: Australian lawmaker loses both legs in vehicle attack as suspect appears in court  NBC News'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken  BBCAustralian politician who was intentionally hit by car loses both her legs  CBS NewsAustralian Politicians Were Already on Edge Before One of Their Own Was Attacked  The New York TimesSoft-spoken David Pocock has big ambitions – but first he wants politicians to ‘double down’ on kindness &...
articles.full_text:
SYDNEY — Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs amputated after being rammed by a car outside her electoral office, her husband said Wednesday, as the man accused of the attack appeared in court.
Doctors amputated Haines’ left leg after the alleged attacker struck her twice with his car in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, on Monday, Phil Haines said. They worked for days to save her right leg but were ultimately unsuccessful, he told a news conference in Melbourne.
“The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” he said.
Australian lawmaker loses leg in car ramming attack
Brendan Nugent, a 43-year-old resident of the rural town of Tarrawingee within Haines’ electorate, was charged with three offenses: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and causing harm to a public official.
Additional charges of cannabis cultivation and possession have also been laid against Nugent, court filings showed.
The suspect was restrained by members of the public at the scene before being arrested.
Haines, an independent lawmaker who has championed causes including climate change and regional housing, remains in critical condition.
Police are still investigating the motive for the rare attack on an elected official.
During a brief court appearance Wednesday, Nugent’s lawyer said his client suffers from a rare neurological condition called idiopathic transverse myelitis and was also being treated for concussion, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported. His lawyer told the magistrate his client had some mental health concerns and that it was his first time in custody.
There was no application for bail, and the case was deferred until Feb. 4.
Anti-terrorism police are among the agencies investigating the incident. While police allege the attack was “targeted,” they believe it was an isolated incident.
There was no intelligence to suggest any threat to Haines, and the Australian Federal Police received no warning of any imminent danger from the alleged attacker, Commissioner Krissy Barrett told reporters.
“What I can say is we didn’t have any specific intelligence that would have indicated something as atrocious as happened on Monday afternoon,” she said.
Victoria state police said they could not find any direct past contact between Haines and Nugent, with the motive still unknown.
“Motivation is one of these things that we absolutely need to explore. His motivation for this, what we allege is a deliberate attack, is very much a centerpiece of the investigation,” Victoria Police Chief Mike Bush said.
Bush declined to comment on the man’s mental health, saying the matter was before the court.
Haines had worked in nursing, midwifery and academia before being elected to parliament in 2019 for the rural seat of Indi, which she retained in both 2022 and 2025.
Violent attacks on politicians are rare in Australia, where federal lawmakers, state leaders and even prime ministers are often seen shopping, grabbing coffee or attending community events with relatively little security.
However, concerns about politicians’ safety have grown in recent years amid rising political polarization, online abuse and threats against elected officials, prompting calls for greater protections while preserving the accessibility that has long characterized Australian politics.

articles.title: RBA deputy warns inflation outlook 'materially worse' as next decision looms - ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
articles.summary: RBA deputy warns inflation outlook 'materially worse' as next decision looms  ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

source_detail.name: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

articles.full_text:
In short:
The RBA deputy governor says there are signs some people do not expect inflation to come back to the RBA's target, which is "central banker's nightmare".
Markets are putting the chance of a November rate hike at more than 50 per cent.
What's next?
The RBA's rate-setting board will next meet at the beginning of November, with a decision handed down on Melbourne Cup day.
Reserve Bank deputy governor Andrew Hauser says the inflation outlook is "materially worse" than the RBA had forecast, raising the prospect of another interest rate hike as soon as November.
Just under a fortnight out from the next interest rate decision, Mr Hauser warned high inflation was becoming entrenched in the Australian economy.
"We are beginning to see some signs that some people in the community are not sure if we're going to bring inflation back into target at all, or certainly not for an extended period," Mr Hauser told the Citi Investment Conference in Sydney.
The RBA targets headline inflation between 2 and 3 per cent on average over time.
Inflation currently sits at 4 per cent, according to the August consumer price index.
Mr Hauser said the central bank's liaison program and surveys showed there was "an increasing share of businesses who are thinking that, maybe, sort of 3 per cent, 3.5 per cent [inflation] is the new normal".
"Look, that is the central banker's nightmare.
"We can't allow expectations to shift away from target."
Market pricing now puts the chance of an interest rate hike in November at 51 per cent, based on Bloomberg data.
The odds of a hike next month had dipped below 20 per cent last week, after the unemployment rate reached a five-year high in September.
UBS chief economist George Tharenou described Mr Hauser's remarks as "hawkish" and said the investment bank was forecasting a November rate hike.
"Hauser's comments today are consistent with our view of the likelihood the RBA staff provide an explicit recommendation at the November meeting to raise the cash rate," Mr Tharenou said.
The RBA will release its quarterly forecasts in its Statement on Monetary Policy on November 3, the same day the interest-rate-setting board next hands down a decision.
Betashares chief economist David Bassanese agreed that the RBA official was setting the stage for a Melbourne Cup day hike.
"Despite the steadfast claims that the Reserve Bank is no longer in the business of offering forward guidance, its signals to the market in recent weeks have rarely been clearer," Mr Bassanese said.
"In short, the RBA seems increasingly prepared to risk a recession to get inflation down – given it has been above target for an extended period and it is sensing evidence of rising inflation expectations within the community."
"It remains possible the RBA board vote will be split, and the external members have a majority to hold rates, and hence effectively 'outvote' Bullock and Hauser," Mr Tharenou said.
However, even if the RBA holds rates in November, he still would expect "a 'hawkish hold', with the RBA retaining a tightening bias … and also setting up a hike at the subsequent meeting in December".
'Laying shorter-term pain on top of pain'
Mr Hauser reiterated the "hard choices" facing the RBA as it balanced the pressures on prices from the Middle East crisis, the AI and technology boom and weak productivity growth.
Asked about the pain of higher interest rates hitting many households, on top of cost-of-living pressure, the deputy governor said: "It's a continuous challenge to explain this."
"The reason is that, even though we are laying shorter-term pain on top of pain, it's to prevent a longer and potentially far worse pain down the track if inflation expectations get locked in," Mr Hauser said, echoing comments RBA governor Michele Bullock has made as the central bank has lifted rates.
Mr Hauser downplayed concerns about the state of the jobs markets, saying there was potentially "noise" in the numbers, after the unemployment rate rose to 4.7 per cent in September.
"That said, it clearly was a little weaker than we and others have been expecting," he said.
"I stress the 'little'. These unemployment numbers in Australia are still right at the bottom or very near the bottom of G20 out-turns on labour markets."
He said "no lost job is one to celebrate" but the labour market needed to soften.
"We need to see some easing in the economy, whether [the unemployment rate] goes to 5 [per cent], whether it goes to some other number," Mr Hauser said.
"That's a debate we're having in the context of our forecast at the moment, and you'll see our answers to that in a week or two."

articles.summary: BT Explainer: The companies behind the brands: Why product design could be India's next manufacturing opportunity  Business Today
articles.full_text:
India's manufacturing boom is opening a new opportunity for the companies that make products for global brands: moving beyond assembly to designing, engineering and developing the products themselves. As global companies diversify their supply chains, Indian original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) are looking to move up the value chain, where technology, product development and component-level expertise could offer greater opportunities than manufacturing scale alone.
The shift comes as India's electronics manufacturing industry has expanded from ₹1.9 lakh crore in FY15 to approximately ₹12 lakh crore in FY25, while the auto components industry reached ₹6.73 lakh crore in FY25. But higher output does not automatically translate into greater value capture for domestic suppliers. The next phase of growth will depend on whether Indian manufacturers can move beyond executing orders to contributing to product design, research and development (R&D), engineering and system integration.

articles.title: 2 men rearrested in UK on suspicion of assisting Iran over suspected plot at a US-run air base - AP News
articles.summary: 2 men rearrested in UK on suspicion of assisting Iran over suspected plot at a US-run air base  AP NewsTwo men rearrested on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service in RAF Fairford incident  CNNTwo men rearrested in suspected plot on U.K. air base used by U.S. bombers  The Washington PostTwo men re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran intelligence after RAF Fairford incident  BBCUK police arrest pair on suspicion of helping Iranian intelligen...
articles.full_text:
LONDON (AP) — British police said Tuesday they have rearrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service over a suspected plot at a U.S.-run air base in England last month.
Counter Terrorism Policing said the men, a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual U.K.-Iranian national, were arrested under the National Security Act.
One of the suspects was first arrested on Sept. 27, when the suspected plot against the U.S.-run base at RAF Fairford took place. The air base in western England has been used to bomb Iran during this year’s war.
The second suspect was first arrested on Oct. 1. Until Tuesday the men had been bailed pending more investigation.
Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in three vans at the site, but no explosives.
British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the apparent plot was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, or IRGC.
Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.
Five other men in their 20s were arrested earlier then released on bail pending further investigation. No one has yet been charged.
Laurence Taylor, head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K., said detectives are looking at “many lines of enquiry involved in this hugely complex investigation.”
“This is very much a live investigation, and our evidence gathering continues, but at this time our position remains the same; we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement,” he said in a statement.
“Our investigators are continuing to examine what that level of involvement was and the ambition behind it,” he added.
Last week the head of Britain’s MI5 spy agency warned that both Iran and Russia were expanding their attacks against the U.K., and that the RAF base incident was not unique.
Ken McCallum, who leads the U.K.’s domestic security service, said Tehran is seeking to intensify its attacks in Britain beyond the traditional targets of Iranians opposed to the country’s Islamic authorities.
In all, more than 50 people have been arrested over Iran-linked plots in the past year, McCallum said.

articles.title: Egypt moves toward sending troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend against attacks by Iran-backed Houthis - CBS News
articles.summary: Egypt moves toward sending troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend against attacks by Iran-backed Houthis  CBS NewsSisi says Egypt would defend Saudi territory but rules out attack on Yemen  ReutersEgypt agrees to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against Houthis  PoliticoAnalysis • As Yemen war escalates, Saudi allies draw strict lines on military backing  HaaretzEgyptian Lawmakers Push Back on Sisi’s Request to Send Troops to Saudi Arabia  الحرة
articles.full_text:
Cairo - Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has asked the country's Parliament to authorize the military to help defend Saudi Arabia after Yemen's intensified their attacks on the kingdom, targeting and oil infrastructure.
Al-Sisi stressed that it would be a defensive mission and only if the kingdom requests assistance.
"Egypt will take any measures requested by Saudi Arabia to protect and defend it," al-Sisi said Saturday during a military graduation ceremony.
Under Egypt's Constitution, the president must consult the National Defense Council and obtain approval from two-thirds of Parliament before deploying the armed forces on a combat mission abroad.
On Sunday, al-Sisi chaired a meeting of the National Defense Council, which reviewed what the Egyptian presidency described as the "grave escalations unfolding in the region" and the "unacceptable attacks" against Saudi Arabia.
The council pledged to provide "all necessary and possible forms of support to the sisterly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to defend its security and stability, and to safeguard its resources, territorial integrity, and Islamic holy sites."
Egypt has managed, so far, to stay out of all the recent military conflicts in the region and has tried to de-escalate and find political solutions. For some, this is one of al-Sisi's greatest achievements.
But Samir Ragheb, a retired army brigadier and political and strategic analyst, told CBS News that it was time for Egypt to make good on commitments it had made to helping secure the region.
"Egypt has repeatedly pledged to support the security of the Gulf states and has issued numerous statements reaffirming this commitment," Ragheb said. "However, this is a time of war, not politics and statements. If Egypt fails to deliver on these promises, they will lose their meaning and amount to nothing more than empty threats."
"The Gulf states have invested billions of dollars in Egypt. Morally, it's Egypt's turn to return the favor," he said.
Parliament convened an emergency session on Sunday and was expected to approve the resolution on Tuesday, but the vote was postponed until next Monday.
The Egyptian Social Democratic Party instructed its parliamentary bloc to abstain from voting on the resolution, saying in a statement it had not received sufficient information about "the mission's scope, costs, and risks, as well as the arrangements in place to protect Egyptian forces."
Ragheb is certain the region is heading toward a more severe escalation.
"Egypt is not going to defend the kingdom against the Houthis," he said. "The threat is much bigger than the Houthis. This includes Iran, Iraqi militias and sleeper cells within the kingdom itself."
However, he also believes Egypt will lose much of its influence in the region if it doesn't intervene.
"If you want to be a regional player, you must play a role," he said. "Otherwise, you will lose your seat at the table."
Ragheb argued that the United States' in support of Saudi Arabia created a vacuum that must be filled by others. He said Egypt should take on the Arab share of that role.
Other regional powers are also trying to fill the vacuum. In August, Saudi Arabia signed a joint defense agreement with Turkey and Pakistan known as the Mecca Accords.
"Even before Saudi Arabia asked for Egyptian support, the Mecca Accords was a death certificate for the idea of relying on America for any form of defense," Ragheb said.

articles.title: 5 priority actions to enhance the position of Vietnamese wood and increase export value. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: 5 priority actions to enhance the position of Vietnamese wood and increase export value.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Large potential but increasing competitive pressure.
 In 2025, exports of wood and wood products are expected to reach approximately $17.2 billion. In the first nine months of 2026, this figure is projected to reach approximately $13.43 billion, a 6.3% increase compared to the same period of the previous year.
 At the trade promotion briefing conference in October 2026, held on the afternoon of October 20th with the theme "Diversifying markets, promoting the export of Vietnamese wood and furniture products," Mr. Phung Quoc Man, Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City Handicraft and Wood Processing Association (HAWA), stated that Vietnamese wood products are present in 167 countries and territories. Vietnam currently ranks second in the world for furniture exports, after China , with a diverse supply capacity ranging from home, office, and outdoor furniture to products for construction projects and hotels.
 According to Mr. Ngo Sy Hoai, Vice President and General Secretary of the Vietnam Wood and Forest Products Association, the wood industry has formed a relatively complete ecosystem from forest planting, harvesting, processing to export. There are approximately 6,000 businesses operating in the industry nationwide, of which more than 3,500 focus on exports, including over 700 foreign-invested enterprises (FDI).
 However, the industry remains heavily reliant on the US market, which typically accounts for over 50% of export revenue. Tariff policies and trade protection measures in this market are putting pressure on businesses. High logistics costs, traceability requirements, and regulations on preventing forest degradation also pose increasing challenges. 
 Mr. Le Hoang Tai, Deputy Director of the Trade Promotion Department (Ministry of Industry and Trade), believes that diversifying markets is not only about seeking more orders but also about enhancing product value and competitiveness. Businesses need to consolidate traditional markets, exploit potential markets, and at the same time understand customer needs, import conditions, and appropriate access channels.
 Several markets are opening up notable opportunities. In the Netherlands , in the first nine months of 2026, Vietnam's exports of wood and wood products reached US$138 million, an 86% increase compared to the same period the previous year. The Netherlands is also a logistics and distribution hub for goods entering the EU. Meanwhile, the Indian furniture market is estimated to be worth approximately US$22 billion, projected to reach US$30-40 billion in the near future, with an average annual growth rate of 8-10%.
 However, according to Mr. Bui Trung Thuong, Vietnam's Commercial Counselor in India , India is also a difficult market to access due to protectionist policies for domestic production and technical barriers. The most-favored-nation import duty on furniture is 20%, while goods from countries with free trade agreements with India, including ASEAN, enjoy a duty rate of 0-5%. Businesses also need to be aware of trade defense measures and certification requirements from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). 
 Mr. Bui Trung Thuong - Commercial Counselor of Vietnam in India. (Screenshot)
 Five priorities to elevate the status of Vietnamese wood.
 To enhance his position in the global value chain, Mr. Ngo Sy Hoai proposed five priority actions.
 Firstly, diversify markets, customers, and sales channels, reducing dependence on a single market. In the US, businesses need to maintain market share, manage tariff and origin risks, and seek new markets, including niche markets. In the EU and UK, they should leverage free trade agreements; in Japan and South Korea , they should expand opportunities for interior and exterior products. Businesses should also explore potential in the Middle East, ASEAN, Australia, and other markets.
 Secondly, investing in design, technology, artificial intelligence (AI), productivity, and human resource skills will gradually shift from contract manufacturing to proactively developing products and owning the brand.
 Thirdly, developing large-timber plantations ensures the legality and traceability of raw materials, meeting the increasingly high demands of importing markets.
 Fourth, build the brand of Vietnamese wood and furniture, and develop direct distribution channels to enhance the value that businesses receive from exported products.
 Fifth, harmoniously link product groups from wood chips, pellets, wood panels to furniture, thereby increasing the value obtained per cubic meter of wood.
 According to Mr. Hoai, the industry needs to shift from purely OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) to ODM (Original Design Manufacturer), aiming for brand ownership. The goal is to create "Made in Vietnam" products, designed by Vietnamese people, bearing Vietnamese brands, and trusted by international customers. 
 Mr. Phung Quoc Man - Chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City Handicraft and Wood Processing Association (HAWA). (Screenshot)  To achieve these priorities, the supportive role of the Vietnamese trade office system abroad is crucial. Mr. Phung Quoc Man suggested that trade offices provide focused information on market needs, customer segments, distribution channels, and import requirements; verify partners; connect businesses with importers and retailers; and monitor the cooperation process from sample submission and quotation to negotiation and order signing.
 Associations and businesses also need to coordinate closely with the Trade Promotion and Business Office to promote production capabilities, attract international buyers to Vietnam to attend specialized trade fairs and exhibitions, and conduct factory surveys.
 According to Mr. Le Hoang Tai, market diversification needs to go hand in hand with enhancing competitiveness and participating more deeply in the value-creating stages of the supply chain. This is also a direction consistent with the "Go Global" program for the period 2026–2030, approved by Decision No. 626/QD-TTg dated June 4, 2026.
 The ultimate goal is not only to bring more wood products to the international market, but also to help Vietnamese brands become more clearly recognized, enabling businesses to be more proactive in the value chain and benefit proportionally to their production capacity.
 Nguyet Minh

|  The export revenue of Autotech Vietnam Machinery Manufacturing Joint Stock Company (VSIP Industrial Park) has grown significantly. | 
 Mr. Chan Yan Tao, Deputy General Director of Micro Commercial Components Vietnam Co., Ltd. (Yen Phong II-C Industrial Park), said: The company is gradually shifting from manufacturing electronic components to manufacturing semiconductor devices to increase added value; in the first six months of 2026, it contributed nearly 207,200 USD to the local budget.
 Samsung Electronics Vietnam Co., Ltd. (Yen Phong I Industrial Park) is one of the foreign direct investment (FDI) enterprises playing a core role in Bac Ninh's export growth. Mr. Kim Yong Sup, Deputy General Director in charge of External Relations of the company, said: “The company is continuously expanding its production scale, modernizing its equipment lines, promoting the shift in the local economic structure towards modern industry, and creating conditions for domestic enterprises to participate more deeply in the global supply chain. In the first nine months of 2026, the company's revenue is estimated to reach VND 386.9 trillion, an increase of 16%.”
 Efficiently operating businesses have created a crucial foundation for Bac Ninh to maintain its import and export growth momentum, with a total turnover estimated at US$177.8 billion. Of this, exports reached US$87.5 billion, an increase of over 30.5% compared to the same period last year, continuing to hold the top position nationwide. Key products experiencing exceptional growth in production volume include semiconductors (up 2.1 times), smartphones (up 2.02 times), peripherals (up 1.44 times), and smartwatches (up 1.22 times).
 According to the Director of the Department of Industry and Trade, Nguyen Minh Hieu, in 2026, businesses continuously expanded their production scale, benefiting from the positive impact of the global investment capital shift towards high-tech sectors, which are Bắc Ninh's strengths. Therefore, the production of key product groups such as telephones, computers, electronic products, and components increased significantly, contributing to the growth of export value in the first nine months.
 A bright spot from domestic businesses.
 Besides FDI enterprises, many domestic businesses have made breakthroughs in export value, contributing positively to the trade surplus and creating jobs for tens of thousands of workers. 
 At Bac Giang Garment Corporation (LGG), export value increased by 12% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period last year. LGG aims for an annual export revenue of $170 million, creating stable jobs for nearly 7,000 workers with an average income of VND 14 million per person per month. According to Mr. Nguyen Van Tu, Deputy General Director of the company, the enterprise has invested approximately VND 250 billion in building a smart factory to improve productivity, reduce costs, shorten delivery times, and meet the increasingly high demands of international partners. Several major partners have proposed increasing their order volume by about 50%. The company's products are currently present in many demanding markets such as the US, Europe, Japan, and South Korea .
 Autotech Vietnam Machinery Manufacturing Joint Stock Company (VSIP Industrial Park) provides automation solutions for manufacturing industries such as electronics, automotive, food, and beverages. The company supplies many large domestic and international corporations such as Samsung, Dreamtech, Vinfast, Nidec, P&G, etc. Currently, Autotech is expanding its exports to countries such as the United States , Canada, Mexico, Japan, India, and South Korea. To improve productivity and product quality, the company has reorganized its entire production process towards a smart factory. In the first nine months of 2026, the company's revenue reached over VND 600 billion, an increase of 30%, with export revenue increasing by 20%.
 Affirming its position as a growth pole
 Assessing the current context, Dr. Nguyen Phuong Bac, former Director of the Bac Ninh Institute for Economic and Social Development Research, commented: With the complex developments in global trade, unpredictable changes in tariffs and supply chains, Bac Ninh needs to continue diversifying its markets and effectively utilizing new-generation free trade agreements (FTAs) to maintain its leading position in exports. It also needs strong support mechanisms to enable domestic businesses to participate more deeply in the supply chains of FDI corporations.
 Furthermore, relevant authorities need to provide better support to businesses regarding market information, technical standards, and market access conditions; businesses need to improve their production capacity, build brands, and strengthen import-export connections with logistics infrastructure; and promote connections between import-export businesses and logistics service providers to enhance efficiency and competitiveness throughout the entire chain. 
|  | 
|  Yen Phong II-C Industrial Park has a comprehensive infrastructure that meets the requirements of investors. | 
 Emphasizing the development orientation, Mr. Ngo Tan Phuong, Vice Chairman of the People's Committee of Bac Ninh City, affirmed: Bac Ninh is creating the most favorable conditions to attract high-quality investment capital into the electronics, semiconductor, artificial intelligence, and high-tech industries. Maintaining its leading position nationwide in export turnover is a solid foundation for Bac Ninh to continue to rise, affirming its position as a dynamic, innovative, and deeply integrated economy.
 With the current growth momentum, authorities estimate that by 2026, Bac Ninh's total import and export turnover will reach 200 billion USD. Vice Chairman of the Bac Ninh City People's Committee, Ngo Tan Phuong, stated: "The city leadership has agreed with the Customs Department's proposal to organize an event to announce this historic milestone when Bac Ninh's import and export turnover reaches 200 billion USD."

articles.title: [C-Shock, K-Industry on the Brink | Cosmetics] China Takes a 'Big Step' to No. 5 Globally, Closes in on K-Beauty - 아시아경제
articles.summary: [C-Shock, K-Industry on the Brink | Cosmetics] China Takes a 'Big Step' to No. 5 Globally, Closes in on K-Beauty  아시아경제
articles.full_text:
[C-Shock, K-Industry on the Brink | Cosmetics] China Takes a 'Big Step' to No. 5 Globally, Closes in on K-Beauty
Color Cosmetics Exports Nearly 2.9 Times Korea's
Skincare Also Enters U.S. Retail Networks
Imports into Korea Also Up 26.6%
"C-beauty is just as important to us as K-beauty."
Kecia Steelman, CEO of Ulta Beauty, the largest beauty retailer in the United States, made the remark during a conference call on the company's second-quarter fiscal 2026 results on August 27 (local time). Asked how the company would stay competitive as more retailers began selling K-beauty products, she unexpectedly brought up Chinese cosmetics. Citing Chinese skincare brand Proya, she emphasized the importance of C-beauty.
Proya will begin selling its products next month at 400 Ulta Beauty stores and through the retailer's online store. It will be the first Chinese premium skincare brand to join Ulta Beauty's online and offline distribution networks simultaneously. C-beauty, which had drawn attention for its ornate packaging and color cosmetics, is now targeting the U.S. market with skincare products that emphasize benefits such as skin firmness and barrier care.
Chinese cosmetics companies are expanding beyond their domestic market into the global marketplace. As more brands enter global distribution networks, China has also climbed the export rankings. With competition extending into skincare, an area where South Korea has traditionally been strong, K-beauty brands are now facing Chinese competitors both on overseas shelves and in their home market.
People enter the Flower Knows pop-up store in Seongsu-dong, Seoul. Courtesy of Flower Knows' social media.
View original image
Fifth in global exports...color cosmetics exports nearly triple South Korea's
According to the Korea International Trade Association on October 22, China's cosmetics exports totaled KRW 813.72 billion from January to July, up 24.3% from KRW 654.48 billion in the same period last year. China rose from seventh in the annual export rankings last year to fifth for January to July this year. Italy and Spain, which ranked above China last year, exported KRW 773.33 billion and KRW 761.81 billion, respectively, during the same period this year.
South Korea ranked second with KRW 1.10246 trillion, behind France at KRW 1.98204 trillion. China's exports amounted to 73.8% of South Korea's. The gap narrowed from 63.6% on an annual basis last year. The figures cover not only cosmetics but also perfumes, hair products, and skin-cleansing products such as body wash. When the scope is narrowed to cosmetics (HS 3304), including skincare and color cosmetics, China's exports totaled KRW 413.11 billion, ranking fourth globally. France led with KRW 996.37 billion, followed by South Korea with KRW 905.74 billion and the United States with KRW 439.85 billion.
China has already overtaken South Korea in color cosmetics. From January to July this year, China's exports of four product categories—lip and eye makeup, powders, and nail products—totaled KRW 187.43 billion, about 2.9 times South Korea's KRW 64.47 billion. China exported KRW 72.74 billion in lip makeup, 1.7 times South Korea's KRW 41.63 billion, and KRW 54.77 billion in eye makeup, 3.5 times South Korea's KRW 15.53 billion. The two countries also differed in growth rates. China's exports increased 17% to 33% across all four categories from a year earlier. By contrast, South Korea's exports of lip makeup fell 15%, while nail product exports declined 15.6%.
Building online recognition before expanding into overseas brick-and-mortar stores
Chinese brands are building recognition online before moving into brick-and-mortar stores overseas. Their strategy is to attract consumers not only with low prices but also with distinctive designs and product assortments.
Color cosmetics brand Flower Knows has made its mark with packaging and decorations reminiscent of objects from fairy tales. Last month, it began a limited-time sale of five signature products at 450 Ulta Beauty stores in the United States. The move came nine months after the brand joined Ulta Beauty's online store in December last year.
Florasis is targeting markets in Japan and Europe with products that incorporate traditional Chinese patterns and craftsmanship. After establishing a sales base on e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, Shopee, and Lazada, it is expanding its distribution channels into premium retail outlets. JUDYDOLL also secured overseas customers through Shopee and TikTok Shop before expanding offline. In December last year, it entered approximately 12,000 FamilyMart stores in Japan. Perfect Diary has made Southeast Asia a base for its overseas expansion. In 2020, it established sales channels in Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines through Shopee.
Expanding into South Korea, with imports up 26.6%
The domestic market is supporting Chinese cosmetics companies' overseas expansion. They are drawing on their domestic customer base and product development experience in their international businesses. According to China's National Bureau of Statistics, retail sales of cosmetics totaled 272.3 billion yuan (approximately KRW 5.41849 trillion) from January to July this year, up 6.3% from the same period last year. This was far above the 1.2% growth in total retail sales of consumer goods over the same period. Retail sales of cosmetics in July also rose 6.8% to 28.5 billion yuan (approximately KRW 567.15 billion), outpacing the 0.6% increase in overall retail sales.
South Korean manufacturers with production bases in China also saw sales grow. Cosmax China's revenue in the first half of this year rose 32.2% year over year to KRW 254.8 billion. Cosmax Guangzhou's revenue also increased 22.7% to KRW 77.3 billion.
Chinese brands are also expanding their distribution networks in South Korea. According to the Korea Customs Service, South Korea's cosmetics imports from China totaled KRW 154.1 billion from January to September this year, up 26.6% from KRW 121.7 billion in the same period last year.
Flower Knows, which entered the South Korean market directly in October last year, launched its official website and operated three pop-up stores over the course of a year. It has also joined Musinsa Beauty, Chicor, and KakaoTalk Gift, among other platforms. Musinsa Beauty also sells other Chinese brands, including AZTK and Into You.
South Korean cosmetics companies have built trust in skincare by emphasizing ingredients and products formulated to be gentle on the skin. Chinese brands, which first drew attention for their color cosmetics and designs, are now supplying major distribution networks with skincare products that highlight their efficacy. Whether Chinese companies, which have accelerated product development and launches, can also earn consumers' trust in their brands is likely to shape the competition ahead.

A cosmetics industry official said, "Their supply chains and speed of product development and launches have reached a level that cannot be ignored, but they still need to catch up with global leaders in brand power and trust in their core research and development (R&D) capabilities. The key will be how quickly they can turn that into consumer trust."

AGENCY:
Bureau of Indian Affairs, Interior.
                    SUMMARY:
The Department of the Interior (Department) gives notice that the group known as the Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation, a petitioner for Federal acknowledgment as an American Indian Tribe, has chosen to complete the petitioning process under the current version of the acknowledgment regulations and has supplemented its petition. The Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation had been proceeding under a previous version of the regulations (as they existed prior to July 31, 2015). The Department seeks comments and evidence from the public on the supplemented petition.
                    DATES:
Comments and evidence must be postmarked by February 18, 2027.
                    ADDRESSES:
                        Copies of the narrative portion(s) of the supplemented documented petition, as submitted by the petitioner (with any redactions appropriate under 25 CFR 83.21(b)), and other information are available at the Office of Federal Acknowledgement's (OFA) website: 
                        www.bia.gov/as-ia/ofa.
                         Submit any comments or evidence to: Department of the Interior, Office of the Assistant Secretary—Indian Affairs, Attention: Office of Federal acknowledgment, Mail Stop 4071 MIB, 1849 C Street NW, Washington, DC 20240, or by email to: 
                        Ofa_Info@bia.gov.
            
                SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation submitted a documented petition on February 24, 1988, for evaluation under a previous version of the acknowledgment regulations (as they existed prior to July 31, 2015). On July 1, 2015, the Department revised 25 CFR part 83 (80 FR 37862), and the regulations became final and effective on July 31, 2015. Pursuant to 25 CFR 83.7 of the revised regulations, the Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation chose to complete the petitioning process under the revised regulations and has now supplemented its petition.
A key goal of the 2015 revisions was to improve transparency through increased notice of petitions and providing improved public access to petitions. The Department informs the public that the petition submitted by the Juaneño Band of Mission Indians, Acjachemen Nation, which has not yet received a final agency decision, will be evaluated pursuant to the standards and processes set forth in the current regulations. Portions of the supplemented petition are publicly available on the website identified above for easy access, and OFA seeks public comment on the petition.
The contact information for the petitioner is Mr. Nathan Banda, 31411 LaMatanza St., Ste. A, San Juan Capistrano, CA 92675.
Also, OFA publishes on its website the following:
i. The narrative portion(s) of the supplemented documented petition, as submitted by the petitioner (with any redactions appropriate under 25 CFR 83.21(b));
ii. The name, location, and mailing address of the petitioner and other information to identify the entity;
iii. The date of receipt;
iv. The opportunity for individuals and entities to submit comments and evidence supporting or opposing the petitioner's request for acknowledgment within 120 days of the date of the website posting; and
v. The opportunity for individuals and entities to request to be kept informed of general actions regarding a specific petitioner.
Authority
The Department publishes this notice and request for comment in the exercise of authority delegated by the Secretary of the Interior to the Assistant Secretary—Indian Affairs by Department Manual part 209, chapter 8.
                    William Henry Kirkland III,
Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs.
